title: Reviving Error Correction in Modern Deep Time-Series Forecasting
summary: Modern deep-learning models have achieved remarkable success in time-series forecasting. Yet, their performance degrades in long-term prediction due to error accumulation in autoregressive inference, where predictions are recursively used as inputs. While classical error correction mechanisms (ECMs) have long been used in statistical methods, their applicability to deep learning models remains limited or ineffective. In this work, we revisit the error accumulation problem in deep time-series forecasting and investigate the role and necessity of ECMs in this new context. We propose a simple, architecture-agnostic error correction model that can be integrated with any existing forecaster without requiring retraining. By explicitly decomposing predictions into trend and seasonal components and training the corrector to adjust each separately, we introduce the Universal Error Corrector with Seasonal-Trend Decomposition (UEC-STD), which significantly improves correction accuracy and robustness across 4 backbones and 10 datasets. Our findings provide a practical tool for enhancing forecasts while offering new insights into mitigating autoregressive errors in deep time-series models. Code is available at https://github.com/DA2I2-SLM/UEC-STD.
core_methodology: The core contribution is the Universal Error Corrector with Seasonal-Trend Decomposition (UEC-STD), an architecture-agnostic mechanism that explicitly decomposes predictions into trend and seasonal components and trains a dedicated corrector module to adjust each separately. This method is designed to mitigate the error accumulation found in autoregressive deep learning inference without retraining the base forecaster.
data_sources: The paper tested the method across 10 diverse datasets, likely including various financial and macroeconomic time series, although the abstract does not specify the nature of the datasets beyond reporting performance improvements across them.
alpha_potential: This research directly addresses a critical limitation in deep learning time-series forecasting: error accumulation in multi-step-ahead predictions. In quantitative trading, producing robust, long-horizon forecasts (e.g., for quarterly factors, monthly return expectations, or macro forecasts) is crucial for strategy formulation and risk management. By significantly improving the robustness and accuracy of deep forecasts—especially over longer horizons—this tool offers a direct pathway to generating more reliable predictive signals for momentum, factor rotation, or trend-following strategies. The architecture-agnostic nature means it can be immediately applied to existing deep learning models used for alpha generation.
title_cn: 复兴现代深度时间序列预测中的误差校正
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种名为UEC-STD的通用误差校正器，用于解决深度学习模型在长期自回归预测中误差累积的问题。该方法可无缝集成到现有模型中，通过单独校正趋势和季节性分量显著提高预测精度。这为量化策略提供了更可靠、更鲁棒的长期预测信号，尤其适用于需要高精度多步预测的因子挖掘和动量策略。

title: Dynamic TMoE: A Drift-Aware Dynamic Mixture of Experts Framework for Non-Stationary Time Series Forecasting
summary: Non-stationary time series forecasting is challenged by evolving distribution shifts that static models struggle to capture. While Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures offer a promising paradigm for decoupling complex drift patterns, existing approaches are limited by fixed expert pools and memoryless routing, hampering their ability to adapt to abrupt regime shifts. To address this, we propose Dynamic TMoE, a framework that unifies architectural evolution with temporal continuity during learning phase. By detecting distribution shifts via Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), we dynamically instantiate heterogeneous experts and prune redundant ones to optimize capacity. Additionally, a temporal memory router leverages recurrent states and an anomaly repository to ensure stable, context-aware expert selection without requiring test-time updates. Experiments on nine benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, reducing MSE by 10.4% and MAE by 7.8%. Code is available at https://github.com/andone-07/Dynamic-TMoE.
core_methodology: The Dynamic TMoE framework addresses non-stationary time series by employing a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture with dynamic adaptation. It uses Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) for real-time distribution shift detection, allowing for the instantiation of new, specialized experts and the pruning of obsolete ones. A key innovation is the temporal memory router, which uses recurrent states and an anomaly repository to guide expert selection contextually without requiring test-time updates, ensuring stability during regime changes.
data_sources: The abstract specifies 'nine benchmarks,' implying standard time series datasets, likely including financial or economic time series, given the focus on non-stationarity and drift awareness.
alpha_potential: The ability to dynamically adapt to abrupt regime shifts (e.g., market crashes, sudden volatility changes, or factor rotations) is crucial for algorithmic trading. Traditional models fail in these situations. Dynamic TMoE offers a robust mechanism for modeling evolving market dynamics, which can translate directly into adaptive trading signals, improved risk modeling, and better factor forecasting in non-stationary environments. This is highly relevant for strategies that rely on regime identification.
title_cn: 动态TMoE：一种用于非平稳时间序列预测的漂移感知的动态专家混合框架
summary_cn: 该研究提出了动态TMoE框架，通过动态实例化和剪枝异构专家，结合最大均值差异（MMD）检测分布漂移，以解决金融市场固有的非平稳性问题。其时间记忆路由器能稳定地进行专家选择。该方法在处理突发市场状态转变方面具有显著优势，可用于构建对市场结构变化具有更强鲁棒性的自适应交易模型和信号生成器。

title: The General Theory of Localization Methods
summary: This paper proposes a general machine learning framework called the localization method, which is fundamentally built on two core concepts: localization kernels and local means -- key components that underpin the self-attention mechanism. To establish a rigorous theoretical foundation, the framework is formally defined through two essential pillars: the formulation of the local(-ized) model and the localization trick. We systematically investigate the connections between the localization method and a wide range of existing machine learning models/methods, including (but not limited to) kernel methods, lazy learning, the MeanShift algorithm, relaxation labeling, Hopfield networks, local linear embedding (LLE), fuzzy inference, and denoising autoencoders (DAEs). By dissecting these relationships, we clarify the broader theoretical significance of the localization method and demonstrate its practical applicability across diverse machine learning tasks. Furthermore, we explore advanced extensions of the framework, such as adaptive kernels, hierarchical local models, and non-local models. Notably, we show that the Transformer -- a cornerstone of modern sequence modeling -- can be constructed using hierarchical local models, revealing the ability of the localization method to unify and generalize state-of-the-art architectures. This work not only provides a unified theoretical lens to reinterpret existing models but also offers new methodological tools for designing flexible, data-adaptive learning systems.
core_methodology: This paper introduces a unified theoretical framework called the 'localization method,' based on localization kernels and local means. It rigorously defines local models and the localization trick, linking this approach to existing ML techniques like kernel methods, Hopfield networks, and DAEs. Crucially, it demonstrates that Transformers can be constructed using hierarchical local models.
data_sources: The framework is generalized for various ML tasks, suggesting applicability to time-series market data (e.g., price, volume, order book data), potentially enhancing feature extraction for trading signals.
alpha_potential: The framework provides a unified theoretical lens for understanding and generalizing sequence modeling architectures, particularly Transformers. Since Transformers are already highly relevant for time-series forecasting and signal extraction in finance, this foundational work offers new methodological tools for designing more flexible, data-adaptive sequence models, which can directly improve predictive power for alpha generation strategies relying on complex temporal dependencies.
title_cn: 定位方法的通用理论
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一个统一的机器学习框架——定位方法，其核心在于局域核和局域均值，并与Transformer架构建立了联系。该理论为构建更灵活、自适应的金融时间序列预测模型提供了新的工具，有助于改进基于序列数据的信号提取和策略预测能力。

title: $ECUAS_n$: A family of metrics for principled evaluation of uncertainty-augmented systems
summary: In high-stakes automated decision-making, access to predictive uncertainty is essential for enabling users -- human or downstream systems -- to accept or reject predictions based on application-specific cost trade-offs. Such uncertainty-augmented (UA) systems -- i.e., systems that output both predictions and uncertainty scores -- are currently being assessed in the literature in a variety of ways, using separate metrics to evaluate the predictions and the uncertainty scores, setting a cost function with a fixed rejection cost or integrating over a coverage-risk curve. We argue that these evaluation approaches are inadequate for assessing overall performance of the UA system for decision making under uncertainty and propose a novel family of metrics, $ECUAS_n$, formulated as proper scoring rules for the task of interest. The parameter $n$ controls the trade-off between the cost of incorrect predictions and imperfect uncertainties depending on the needs of the use-case. We demonstrate the advantages of the $ECUAS_n$ metrics both theoretically and empirically, through experiments on diverse classification and generation datasets, including a manually annotated subset of TriviaQA.
core_methodology: The paper introduces $ECUAS_n$, a novel family of metrics designed specifically for evaluating 'Uncertainty-Augmented' (UA) systems. These metrics are formulated as proper scoring rules, allowing for a principled, unified assessment of both the primary prediction and its associated uncertainty score, controlled by the parameter 'n' to represent application-specific cost trade-offs (e.g., between prediction error and uncertainty calibration).
data_sources: The evaluation is demonstrated on diverse classification and generation datasets, including an annotated subset of TriviaQA. While the examples are not financial, the framework is designed to be data-agnostic, applicable to any time series or sequential data where accurate uncertainty quantification is crucial.
alpha_potential: The primary value lies in building better decision-making components for algorithmic trading systems. In finance, predictions of asset returns or volatility always come with uncertainty. $ECUAS_n$ allows a system designer to rigorously tune the cost of an incorrect trade versus the utility of knowing *when not to trade* (rejection/hedge). This is critical for risk management, portfolio construction (e.g., position sizing based on confidence), and developing adaptive trading agents that can dynamically adjust strategy based on their predicted reliability. It directly enhances the robustness and interpretability of predictive models used for alpha generation.
title_cn: $ECUAS_n$：一套用于系统不确定性增强的原则性评估指标族
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一系列新的$ECUAS_n$指标，用于统一评估预测准确性和不确定性校准的系统性能。在量化交易中，这意味着可以更精确地校准模型（如价格预测或波动率估计）的置信度，从而优化交易决策的时间点和仓位大小。这有助于构建在市场高风险阶段能有效拒绝交易或采取对冲策略的鲁棒性算法。

title: Memory-Induced Supra-Competitive Outcomes Between Deep Reinforcement Learning Agents in Optimal Trade Execution
summary: In this paper, we investigate whether deep reinforcement-learning agents interacting in a shared optimal-execution environment can sustain supra-competitive outcomes, in the sense of achieving lower implementation shortfalls than the relevant game-theoretical competitive benchmark. We study a two-agent Almgren-Chriss liquidation game and examine how learned behavior depends on intra-episode environment feedback, the ability to interpret the mid-price and the agent's knoledge of the past. We first use ex-ante schedule-learning agents to remove intra-episode feedback and isolate what can arise when agents commit to complete liquidation trajectories before execution begins. We then allow agents to condition on the evolving state using a variety of DDQN architectures. We find that, when agents are given access to intra-episode history, especially recent prices and own past actions, supra-competitive outcomes become substantially more frequent and more persistent. These findings indicate that supra-competitive behavior in this execution game is driven not by multi-agent learning or by current price observation alone, but by feedback, memory, and state-contingent interaction along the realized execution path.
core_methodology: The core methodology involves applying Deep Q-Networks (DDQN) to a two-agent optimal trade execution game (Almgren-Chriss model). It specifically investigates the impact of agent memory (access to intra-episode history, past actions, and price evolution) on achieving 'supra-competitive' outcomes (better than a competitive benchmark, i.e., lower implementation shortfall). The research contrasts purely schedule-based learning with state-contingent execution.
data_sources: Simulated market data based on the Almgren-Chriss framework, utilizing intraday price movements, agent actions, and environmental feedback within the context of an optimal execution problem.
alpha_potential: This research directly addresses optimizing trade execution, a critical component of reducing transaction costs (implementation shortfall) for large institutional orders. Finding that memory and state-contingent interaction lead to supra-competitive outcomes suggests that highly adaptive, history-aware RL agents can significantly outperform static benchmarks or simple competitive execution models. This has direct alpha-generating potential by minimizing slippage and realizing better realized prices.
title_cn: 记忆诱导的深度强化学习智能体在最佳交易执行中的超竞争结果
summary_cn: 该研究使用深度强化学习（DDQN）模拟了双智能体最优交易执行（Almgren-Chriss模型）。实验发现，当智能体能够感知内部执行历史、自身过去行动和实时反馈时，它们能显著实现超竞争结果，即实现更低的执行成本（冲击成本）。这表明基于记忆和状态历史的学习型执行代理相比于静态或基准模型，在实际大宗订单执行中具有明显的成本节约潜力。

title: Quantifying Hyperparameter Transfer and the Importance of Embedding Layer Learning Rate
summary: Hyperparameter transfer allows extrapolating optimal optimization hyperparameters from small to large scales, making it critical for training large language models (LLMs). This is done either by fitting a scaling law to the hyperparameters or by a judicious choice of parameterization, such as Maximal Update ($μ$P), that renders optimal hyperparameters approximately scale invariant. In this paper, we first develop a framework to quantify hyperparameter transfer through three metrics: (1) the quality of the scaling law fit, (2) the robustness to extrapolation errors, and (3) the asymptotic loss penalty due to choice of parameterization. Next, we investigate through a comprehensive series of ablations why $μ$P appears to offer high-quality learning rate transfer relative to standard parameterization (SP), as existing theory is inadequate. We find that the overwhelming benefit of $μ$P relative to SP when training with AdamW arises simply from maximizing the learning rate of the embedding layer. In SP, the embedding layer learning rate acts as a bottleneck that induces training instabilities; increasing it by a factor of width to match $μ$P dramatically smooths out training while improving hyperparameter transfer. We also find that weight decay improves the scaling law fits, while, in the fixed token-per-parameter setting, it hurts the robustness of the extrapolation.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a framework to quantify hyperparameter transferability—specifically for learning rates—across different model scales, focusing on how different parameterizations (like Maximal Update, $\mu$P, vs. Standard Parameterization, SP) affect stability and transferability. A key finding is that the advantage of $\mu$P often stems from allowing a much higher learning rate for the embedding layer, which resolves training instabilities in SP setups when using optimizers like AdamW.
data_sources: The research focuses on the training dynamics of large language models (LLMs), utilizing synthetic data derived from training task configurations (model width/scale) rather than traditional financial market data.
alpha_potential: While the paper does not propose a direct trading alpha, its findings are highly relevant for the development and robust training of large-scale AI models (LLMs or Transformers) used in quantitative finance for tasks like sentiment analysis, time-series forecasting, or generating trading signals. Ensuring stable and scalable hyperparameter tuning (especially the learning rate for embedded layers) is critical for deploying performant AI models in production trading systems, reducing overfitting risk during scaling, and improving training efficiency.
title_cn: 量化超参数迁移与嵌入层学习率重要性研究
summary_cn: 该研究揭示了大型模型训练中超参数迁移的量化方法，尤其关注学习率在高维缩放下的稳定性。其成果对金融领域部署高性能AI（如LLM）至关重要，因为它明确指出嵌入层学习率设置不当是导致训练不稳定的关键瓶颈。优化此参数有助于提高金融时间序列模型和量化策略AI的训练效率和鲁棒性，间接支持了更可靠的量化模型开发。

title: Mem-$π$: Adaptive Memory through Learning When and What to Generate
summary: We present Mem-$π$, a framework for adaptive memory in large language model (LLM) agents, where useful guidance is generated on demand rather than retrieved from external memory stores. Existing memory-augmented agents typically rely on similarity-based retrieval from episodic memory banks or skill libraries, returning static entries that often misalign with the current context. In contrast, Mem-$π$ uses a dedicated language or vision-language model with its own parameters, separate from the downstream agent, to generate context-specific guidance for complex tasks. Conditioned on the current agent context, the model jointly decides when to produce guidance and what guidance to produce. We train it with a decision-content decoupled reinforcement learning (RL) objective, enabling it to abstain when generation would not help and otherwise produce concise, useful guidance. Across diverse agentic benchmarks spanning web navigation, terminal-based tool use, and text-based embodied interaction, Mem-$π$ consistently outperforms retrieval-based and prior RL-optimized memory baselines, achieving over 30% relative improvement on web navigation tasks.
core_methodology: The Mem-$\pi$ framework introduces adaptive memory generation for LLM agents using a dedicated model trained via decision-content decoupled Reinforcement Learning (RL). This allows the agent to dynamically decide *when* and *what* contextual guidance to generate, in contrast to static retrieval mechanisms.
data_sources: While the paper focuses on agentic benchmarks like web navigation and tool use, the underlying mechanism (adaptive memory generation) could be applied to complex sequences of financial data, such as tick data, macroeconomic releases, or high-frequency order book movements.
alpha_potential: The ability of an LLM agent to dynamically generate relevant, context-specific reasoning or 'memory' on-the-fly, rather than relying on fixed retrieval chunks, offers significant potential for developing more sophisticated, state-aware trading agents. This is crucial for multi-step decision-making in complex, noisy environments like financial markets (e.g., navigating complex regulatory changes or synthesizing disparate news sentiment over time). This improves the adaptability of AI-driven analysis pipelines.
title_cn: Mem-$\pi$：通过学习何时以及生成什么来实现的自适应记忆
summary_cn: Mem-$\pi$框架通过强化学习训练专门的模型，使AI交易代理能够动态地判断何时生成、生成何种上下文相关的决策指引，而非依赖静态信息检索。这提高了复杂、多步骤金融决策（如宏观事件分析或高频市场解读）的适应性和有效性，有望增强AI交易策略的鲁棒性。

title: Mind the Sim-to-Real Gap & Think Like a Scientist
summary: Suppose a planner has a pre-trained simulator of a sequential decision problem and the option to run real experiments in the field. The simulator is cheap to query but inherits confounding and drift from its calibration data. Experimentation is unbiased but consumes one real unit per trial. We study when, and how, the planner should supplement the simulator with experiments. We give three results. First, an extended simulation lemma decomposes the simulator's value error into a calibration--deployment shift that randomization can identify and a parametric residual that no further interaction can reduce. Second, the value gap between the simulator-optimal policy and the optimum splits into a local component, on states the deployed policy already visits, and a reachability component, on states it does not. The reachability component stays bounded away from zero at any horizon under purely passive learning. Third, we propose Fisher-SEP, a simulation-aided experimental policy (SEP) that minimizes the posterior predictive variance of a target policy's value, with reward-only and transition-only specializations. Two case studies illustrate the regimes. In a vending-machine supply chain, front-loaded experimentation overtakes posterior updating once the horizon is long enough to amortize the pilot. In an HIV mobile-testing example with a corridor that separates a well-surveilled region from a poorly-surveilled one, only designed exploration reaches the poorly-surveilled region.
core_methodology: The paper addresses the 'sim-to-real' gap in sequential decision-making (Reinforcement Learning) by providing bounds and an active learning policy (Fisher-SEP). It decomposes the value error into identifiable calibration shifts and fundamental parametric residuals. The key is balancing cheap but potentially biased simulation training with expensive but unbiased real-world experimentation.
data_sources: The study uses simulated environments modeling sequential decision problems, calibrated using 'calibration data' (analogous to historical trading data or a backtesting engine), and verified via direct 'real experiments' (analogous to live trading or paper trading). Applications move beyond standard inputs to focus on environment dynamics.
alpha_potential: This is highly relevant for building robust Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents for trading. In finance, simulators (often based on historical features or simplified models) frequently misrepresent the true market dynamics (drift, confounding factors). The Fisher-SEP framework offers a principled way to design exploration (live experimentation) that specifically targets the parts of the state space where the simulator is most likely wrong (the 'reachability component'), leading to an RL policy transferable to live markets with better performance than purely simulation-trained or passively updated agents.
title_cn: 关注模拟到现实的差距并像科学家一样思考
summary_cn: 该研究提出了在模拟训练和真实世界实验之间取得平衡的策略，解决了强化学习模型在金融市场部署中的“模拟到现实”差距。Fisher-SEP算法指导交易代理人以最小化价值预测方差的方式进行主动探索，能更有效地识别和修正由模型或数据漂移引起的性能损失（价值差距），从而提高基于RL的交易策略的稳健性和实际表现。

title: torchtune: PyTorch native post-training library
summary: Modern LLMs typically require multistage training pipelines to achieve strong downstream performance, with post-training serving as the main interface for adapting open-weight models. We introduce torchtune, a PyTorch-native library designed to streamline the post-training lifecycle of LLMs, enabling efficient fine-tuning, experimentation, and deployment-oriented workflows. Unlike many existing fine-tuning frameworks, which often optimize for ease of use, specialized recipes, or hardware efficiency at the cost of transparency and extensibility, torchtune emphasizes modularity, hackability, and direct access to the underlying PyTorch components. In this paper, we present the design principles behind torchtune, describe how they are reflected in its model builders, training recipes, and distributed training stack, and evaluate the library across representative post-training settings. We compare against popular fine-tuning frameworks, including Axolotl and Unsloth, and show that torchtune provides strong performance and memory efficiency across many settings while remaining flexible enough for rapid research iteration. These results position torchtune as a practical foundation for reproducible LLMs post-training research.
core_methodology: The paper introduces torchtune, a PyTorch-native library focused on streamlining the post-training lifecycle of Large Language Models (LLMs), emphasizing modularity, hackability, and efficiency for fine-tuning, experimentation, and deployment. It provides standardized recipes and a robust distributed training stack, aiming for performance comparable to specialized frameworks while maintaining flexibility.
data_sources: The primary focus is on infrastructure for training and fine-tuning LLMs, which would subsequently be applied to financial data for various financial tasks (e.g., sentiment analysis, news parsing, report generation).
alpha_potential: torchtune itself is an infrastructure tool rather than a direct alpha signal generator. However, by providing a highly efficient, flexible, and reproducible framework for developing and deploying state-of-the-art LLMs (e.g., for sentiment analysis on news/social media, risk assessment from 10-K/Q filings, or generating trading hypotheses), it significantly accelerates the research lifecycle necessary for discovering and implementing sophisticated LLM-based alpha factors.
title_cn: torchtune：PyTorch 原生训练后处理库
summary_cn: 该论文介绍了 torchtune 库，它是一个为高效微调和部署大型语言模型设计的 PyTorch 原生工具。虽然本身不产生阿尔法信号，但它能显著加速研究人员开发、实验和部署基于 LLM 的金融应用（如新闻情绪分析、财报摘要和风险建模）的速度，从而间接提高量化策略的竞争力。

title: Gaussian Sheaf Neural Networks
summary: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have become the de facto standard for learning on relational data. While traditional GNNs' message passing is well suited for vector-valued node features, there are cases in which node features are better represented by probability distributions than real vectors. Concretely, when node features are Gaussians, characterized by a mean and a covariance matrix, naively concatenating their parameters into a single vector and applying standard message passing discards the geometric and algebraic structure that governs means and covariances. We propose Gaussian Sheaf Neural Networks (GSNNs), a principled framework that incorporates these inductive biases into graph-based learning. Building on the theory of cellular sheaves, we derive a new Laplacian operator that generalizes the sheaf Laplacian to this setting and preserves its key properties. We complement our theoretical contributions with experiments on synthetic and real-world data that illustrate the practical relevance of GSNNs.
core_methodology: The core methodology introduces Gaussian Sheaf Neural Networks (GSNNs), extending traditional Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to handle node features represented by probability distributions (specifically Gaussians defined by mean and covariance). It builds a new sheaf Laplacian operator to properly encode the geometric structure of these distributions during message passing.
data_sources: The paper focuses on synthetic and real-world data where node features are inherently probabilistic (Gaussians). In finance, this translates to time series of returns, volatility, correlation matrices, or learned embeddings that are naturally modeled as distributions.
alpha_potential: This framework is highly relevant for modeling complex relational data in finance where features are stochastic. For instance, modeling asset relationships where features are not just point estimates but full covariance/risk profiles. It could significantly enhance portfolio optimization and risk management by respecting the geometry of uncertainty (covariance structures) during graph-based feature aggregation, potentially leading to more robust factor models or inter-market arbitrage strategies.
title_cn: 高斯层聚合神经网络
summary_cn: GSNNs为GNNs处理节点特征为高斯分布（均值和协方差）的场景提供了理论框架。这对于金融市场中处理资产收益率分布、相关性矩阵或风险敞口等非向量特征至关重要。该方法能更精确地在图结构中聚合不确定性信息，有望改进基于图的投资组合优化和风险因子建模的鲁棒性和表现。

title: Portfolio Preference Elicitation in Institutional Crossing Markets
summary: Institutional crossing platforms face a hidden-information problem: investors value trades as portfolios, but liquidity discovery is typically organized around individual securities. We model portfolio crossing as limited-communication preference elicitation over signed portfolio trades. The platform first uses price-directed demand queries to search the portfolio space and then verifies selected packages through value queries; an incumbent verification query records the demand-discovered allocation before further exploration. Final allocations are chosen from elicited reports, so the learning model guides queries but does not determine welfare. The analysis shows why search and verification are complementary. Demand queries locate high-value regions of a nonseparable portfolio space, but they provide only conservative welfare evidence unless selected packages are verified. Value queries provide exact welfare comparisons, but they are ineffective when applied to poorly targeted packages. Market-calibrated experiments using equity panels from the United States, Korea, Japan, and Germany show that demand-only and value-only designs recover only about half of full-information welfare under a limited query budget, whereas the hybrid procedure recovers 88\% and approaches 95\% as communication expands. We then compare exact security-level packages with factor-completed basket packages within the same allocation rule. Security-level packages are the unadjusted-efficiency mode when exact-securities disclosure is inexpensive. Factor-completed baskets become preferable when pretrade message informativeness is costly. The results characterize portfolio crossing as a selective verification problem and identify disclosure-sensitive package representation as a core design choice for hidden liquidity platforms.
core_methodology: The core methodology involves developing a hybrid preference elicitation protocol for portfolio trades in crossing networks, combining price-directed demand queries (search) and value queries (verification). This models portfolio crossing as a selective verification problem under limited communication.
data_sources: Market-calibrated experiments use equity panels from the United States, Korea, Japan, and Germany, focusing on order book or trade execution data within institutional crossing platforms.
alpha_potential: The research directly addresses microstructure issues in institutional trading, specifically liquidity discovery for portfolio trades. While not directly generating traditional alpha signals (like momentum), optimizing the execution of large, complex, multi-security trades (portfolio execution) by minimizing information leakage and maximizing fill quality under communication constraints offers significant cost-saving and efficiency gains, which translates directly to bottom-line performance for institutional traders and execution algorithms. The comparison between security-level and factor-completed basket representation also suggests superior ways to package trades for execution.
title_cn: 机构跨市场中的投资组合偏好征询
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种在机构配对交易中发现隐藏流动性的混合查询机制，有效解决了投资组合交易的隐性信息问题。通过结合价格导向需求查询和价值验证查询，该混合方案在有限沟通预算下能高效地发现高价值的投资组合成交机会，显著优于单一策略。这对于优化大宗、多资产组合的执行效率和降低交易成本具有重要实践指导意义。

title: Fast and Stable Triangular Inversion for Delta-Rule Linear Transformers
summary: Linear attention has emerged as a cornerstone for efficient long-context architectures, as evidenced by its integration into state-of-the-art open-source models including Qwen3.5/3.6, Kimi Linear, and RWKV-7. Models that incorporate linear attention layers with the so-called Delta-Rule involve the inversion of triangular matrices as a core sub-routine. This operation often forms a performance bottleneck, and, due to its high-sensitivity to numerical errors, it can significantly deteriorate end-to-end model accuracy if it is not carefully implemented. This work provides a systematic analysis of both direct and iterative triangular inversion algorithms, targeting methods that are rich in matrix products, and, therefore, have the potential to efficiently utilize modern hardware. To that end, our analysis covers a broad spectrum of mathematical and practical aspects, with a heavy focus on numerical stability, computational complexity, and, ultimately, hardware efficiency and practical considerations. We provide a rigorous experimental evaluation to verify these properties in practical scenarios, and in low-precision floating-point representations, highlighting the strengths and limitations of each method. Performance benchmarks on NPUs reveal up to $4.3\times$ speed-up against the state-of-the-art implementations of SGLang for triangular matrix inversion, leading to significant performance improvements on the entire layer level, while maintaining full end-to-end model accuracy.
core_methodology: This paper focuses on optimizing the numerical stability and computational efficiency of triangular matrix inversions, a critical subroutine in Delta-Rule Linear Transformers. It systematically analyzes direct and iterative inversion algorithms, emphasizing hardware utilization and low-precision performance.
data_sources: Not explicitly detailed, but the methodology is aimed at expediting the computational pipeline for sequence modeling architectures (like LLMs/Transformers) used in processing financial time series data or text-based market sentiment.
alpha_potential: While the paper does not propose a specific trading strategy, the massive speed-up (up to 4.3x) achieved for inference suggests that deploying complex, long-context Transformer models for real-time financial tasks (e.g., high-frequency arbitrage analysis, large-scale event parsing, or complex time-series forecasting) becomes significantly more feasible. Faster model execution directly translates to lower latency in generating trading signals.
title_cn: 三角矩阵求逆的快速与稳定性改进：面向Delta-Rule线性Transformer
summary_cn: 该研究通过系统性分析和优化三角矩阵求逆算法，显著提升了Delta-Rule线性Transformer的计算效率（最高提速4.3倍），解决了数值稳定性和性能瓶颈。在量化交易中，这意味着可以更快速、更准确地部署大型语言模型进行高频信号生成、实时风险分析或大规模文本/市场数据处理，从而降低决策延迟。

title: Stochastic MeanFlow Policies: One-Step Generative Control with Entropic Mirror Descent
summary: Online off-policy reinforcement learning (RL) is shaped by two coupled choices: the policy class and the update rule. Gaussian policies are fast and have tractable entropy, but struggle with multimodal action distributions. Generative policies are more expressive, but often require iterative sampling or lack tractable entropy estimates. On the optimisation side, SAC-style soft policy improvement and mirror descent (MD) can be viewed as minimising different KL divergences: the former moves the policy towards a value-induced Boltzmann distribution, while the latter regularises each update against the previous policy. Combining entropy regularisation with an MD constraint is therefore attractive, as it supports exploration while stabilising policy improvement; however, the resulting target can be multimodal and is poorly matched by unimodal Gaussian policies. We propose Stochastic MeanFlow Policies (SMFP), a one-step generative policy class that maps Gaussian noise to actions through a MeanFlow transformation. This stochastic reparameterisation yields a tractable entropy surrogate and allows MeanFlow policies to be trained within off-policy mirror descent under a unified objective for exploratory yet stable improvement. Across seven MuJoCo benchmarks, SMFP improves over Gaussian and generative baselines while retaining single-step inference efficiency.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Stochastic MeanFlow Policies (SMFP), a novel generative policy class for online off-policy reinforcement learning. It uses a MeanFlow transformation on Gaussian noise to map into actions, enabling tractable entropy estimation while maintaining the expressiveness of generative models. The method is optimized using an off-policy mirror descent (MD) approach, balancing exploration (entropy regularization) with stable policy updates (MD constraint).
data_sources: The evaluation is conducted on MuJoCo benchmarks (simulated control tasks), which primarily tests the sample efficiency and stability of the RL algorithm itself, not direct financial data.
alpha_potential: While the paper tests on MuJoCo simulations, the core contribution—a stable, efficient, and expressive off-policy RL algorithm—is highly relevant for complex trading tasks like high-frequency market making, optimal trade execution, or dynamic portfolio management where action distributions can be multimodal. The improved stability provided by the MD constraint over standard SAC methods would be beneficial in noisy, non-stationary financial environments.
title_cn: 随机均值流策略：具有熵镜面下降的一次性生成控制
summary_cn: 本文提出了随机均值流策略（SMFP），一种用于在线离策略强化学习的新型生成策略。该方法通过均值流变换提高了策略的表达能力和熵的估计可解性，并结合了镜面下降优化以稳定策略改进。该技术路线对构建复杂、高维的金融对齐（如最优执行或动态投资组合）的深度强化学习智能体具有重要借鉴意义。

title: Nonparametric Learning and Earning with One-Point Feedback under Nonstationarity
summary: Firms increasingly rely on dynamic pricing to respond to evolving customer demand, yet in many applications they observe only the revenue generated by a single posted price in each period. At the same time, market conditions may shift gradually or abruptly due to changes in customer preferences, competition, or external shocks. These features create two intertwined challenges: learning the revenue--demand relationship from limited feedback and adapting pricing decisions to a changing environment. We study how a seller can learn and earn effectively under these constraints, without assuming a specific parametric form for demand. We develop a learning framework that updates prices using revenue-based gradient approximations constructed from one observation per period. To address environmental changes, we incorporate a restarting mechanism that periodically refreshes the learning process so that outdated information is discounted. When the degree of nonstationarity is unknown, we further introduce a meta-learning layer to adaptively hedge across multiple restarting schedules. We provide performance guarantees for our approach, showing how cumulative revenue loss relative to a fully informed benchmark depends on both the time horizon and the magnitude of market variation. Simulation experiments using synthetic and real-world data illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed procedures.
core_methodology: The core methodology involves developing a nonparametric learning framework that approximates revenue gradients using only one observation (the realized revenue at a single posted price) per period. It addresses nonstationarity through a periodic restarting mechanism, which discounts outdated information. Furthermore, a meta-learning layer is introduced to adaptively select the optimal restarting schedule when the degree of nonstationarity is unknown.
data_sources: The primary data source is transaction revenue contingent on a single posted price. While the abstract mentions synthetic and real-world data, this model applies to scenarios where price-response data is sparse (one observation per period), similar to how order book data or single trade executions could be conceptualized in a dynamic market setting.
alpha_potential: This framework addresses the challenge of learning optimal actions (pricing/action selection) in dynamic and nonstationary environments using limited feedback (one-point observation). In algorithmic trading, this maps directly to optimizing trade execution decisions (e.g., optimal order size placement, dynamic quoting strategies, or even setting optimal bid/ask spreads) where the true underlying demand curve or market impact function is unknown and constantly shifting. The ability to learn from sparse revenue/profit feedback under nonstationarity offers potential for adaptive microstructure strategies.
title_cn: 非平稳性下基于单点反馈的非参数学习与盈利
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种在市场条件不断变化（非平稳性）且只能观察到单一价格反馈的情况下，学习最优定价或决策的方法。其核心是使用单点观察来近似梯度，并通过重启和元学习机制适应环境变化。这对于高频交易中的动态最优执行、报价策略或任何需要从稀疏、时变信号中快速适应的算法交易场景具有重要的借鉴意义。

title: Divide and Contrast: Learning Robust Temporal Features without Augmentation
summary: Self-supervised learning for time-series representation aims to reduce reliance on labeled data while maintaining strong downstream performance, yet many existing approaches incur high computational costs or rely on assumptions that do not hold across diverse temporal dynamics. In this work, we introduce Divide and Contrast (Di-COT), an unsupervised framework that avoids data augmentation and multiple encoder passes by contrasting informative substructures within a window rather than individual timesteps. Di-COT stochastically partitions each window into a small number of overlapping sub-blocks per iteration, enabling efficient and meaningful contrast while mitigating false positives during temporal transitions. To further improve scalability, we adopt a contrastive objective whose computation depends on the batch size and the number of sub-blocks, making loss computation independent of sequence length. Extensive experiments on six large-scale real-world datasets, as well as the UCR and UEA benchmarks, demonstrate that Di-COT learns semantically structured and transferable representations, achieving state-of-the-art performance on classification, clustering, $k$NN, and cross-dataset transfer, while substantially reducing training time. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/sfi-norwai/Di-COT.
core_methodology: Divide and Contrast (Di-COT) is an unsupervised self-supervised learning framework for time-series representation. It avoids explicit data augmentation by stochastically partitioning a time window into overlapping sub-blocks and contrasting these informative substructures. This ensures efficient contrast learning that is robust to temporal transitions, and its objective scales with batch size rather than sequence length, improving computational efficiency.
data_sources: The paper tests the framework on six large-scale real-world datasets and standard classification/clustering benchmarks (UCR/UEA). In a financial context, these datasets would represent diverse time-series data like high-frequency trading order book snapshots, tick data, or sensor readings converted to time series.
alpha_potential: The core value for quantitative finance lies in Di-COT's ability to learn robust, transferable temporal features without extensive labeling or augmentation. This is crucial for anomaly detection (e.g., market manipulation, fraudulent activities, microstructural events) or learning robust representations of asset price movements or volatility regimes directly from raw, high-dimensional time-series data. The efficiency gains (loss independent of sequence length) make it suitable for processing long streams of tick or order book data for real-time feature engineering, potentially leading to better input features for downstream prediction or RL agents.
title_cn: 划分与对比：在不进行数据增强的情况下学习鲁棒的时间特征
summary_cn: Di-COT 是一种高效的无监督时间序列表征学习框架，通过对比窗口内的子结构来避免数据增强和多重编码器传递。在金融领域，它可以用于从高频或原始市场数据中学习高效、可迁移的鲁棒特征，极大地降低特征工程的计算成本和对标签的依赖度，适用于构建市场异常检测或高质量的策略输入层。

title: Behavior-Consistent Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) often exhibits high variance across training runs, leading to unreliable performance and posing a major challenge to deployment in real-world domains. In this work, we address the challenge of cross-run policy divergence by formalizing the problem of behavior-consistent RL, where the objective is to obtain policies that are both high-performing and distributionally similar across training runs. Our key observation is that maximum-entropy RL provides a direct mechanism for controlling behavioral divergence by anchoring runs to a common (uniform) prior. We prove that, for Boltzmann policies, choosing the temperature proportional to $Q$-function disagreement bounds the pairwise KL divergence between the induced policies. However, we also show that naïvely increasing entropy might impair policy optimization while amplifying off-policy error. Building upon these observations, we propose $Q$-value Expectile Disagreement (QED), a state-dependent temperature schedule that uses double-critic disagreement as a single-run proxy for cross-run disagreement. Empirically, we demonstrate that across 18 continuous-control tasks, QED reduces across-run divergence by two orders of magnitude without sacrificing performance, resulting in a considerable reduction in return variance at modest sample-efficiency costs.
core_methodology: The core methodology introduces 'Behavior-Consistent Deep Reinforcement Learning' to mitigate high variance and policy divergence across training runs in RL agents. It leverages maximum-entropy RL principles and proposes a state-dependent temperature schedule called Q-value Expectile Disagreement (QED), which uses double-critic disagreement as a proxy for cross-run divergence to stabilize training.
data_sources: The paper focuses on continuous-control tasks for general RL stability validation, not specific financial market data. However, the findings are directly applicable to training RL agents using financial time series, order book data, or simulated market environments.
alpha_potential: The direct benefit for quantitative trading is creating much more robust and reliable RL-based trading agents. High variance and poor generalization across training runs are critical barriers to deploying RL in finance (especially for execution or high-frequency strategy learning). By significantly reducing policy divergence (two orders of magnitude reduction in cross-run divergence demonstrated), QED allows practitioners to deploy strategies that are far less sensitive to initial starting conditions or minor data fluctuations, leading to more stable expected returns and better risk management in live trading.
title_cn: 行为一致性深度强化学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出行为一致性深度强化学习（Behavior-Consistent RL）方法，以解决强化学习（RL）模型跨训练运行方差过高、性能不稳定的核心问题。通过引入Q值期望失调（QED）机制，方法能将策略离散度降低两个数量级，同时保持高性能。这对开发高频交易或动态投资组合优化等对模型稳定性要求极高的金融应用，具有显著的实际价值，提高了RL策略部署的可靠性。

title: SURGE: An Event-Centric Social Media Sentiment Time Series Benchmark with Interaction Structure
summary: Public events on social media generate large volumes of discussion whose collective dynamics carry direct value for opinion forecasting and crisis response. Capturing how these dynamics evolve across an event's lifecycle requires organizing fragmented posts into event-level time series. Existing datasets cover only a small number of events within a single category, and typically discard the interaction structure between posts when constructing time series, which restricts both transfer across event types and controlled study of how interactions shape the resulting collective dynamics. We present SURGE, a multi-event social media benchmark that pairs event-level time series with aligned text and interaction structure linking posts within an event. SURGE is built through an automated pipeline that produces calendar-aligned time series at three temporal granularities, covering 67 events and more than 800K posts across five event categories. Each time bin is paired with flat and structured textual views derived from the same selected posts, enabling controlled evaluation of whether social interaction structure affects forecasting behavior. On top of SURGE we define benchmark protocols for numerical-only forecasting, text-augmented forecasting, high-interaction evaluation, and leave-one-category-out generalization. Experiments with representative time-series and multimodal forecasting models reveal three properties of the benchmark: a strong local-persistence regime in which naive baselines remain hard to beat under absolute error, limited transfer of existing text-augmented forecasters to event-driven social-media data, and increased difficulty on reply-dense periods that aggregate metrics tend to obscure. We further include a lightweight structure-aware probe as a reference implementation, illustrating how SURGE can support interaction-aware forecasting research.
core_methodology: The paper introduces SURGE, a benchmark dataset and evaluation framework for event-centric social media time series forecasting. The methodology focuses on organizing social media posts around specific public events, preserving the interaction structure (replies/mentions), and establishing protocols for evaluating numerical-only, text-augmented, and structure-aware forecasting models across multiple event categories.
data_sources: Social media data structured around 67 distinct public events across five categories (>800K posts), providing both textual content and interaction graphs linking posts.
alpha_potential: The core alpha potential lies in generating high-frequency sentiment indicators and opinion forecasts derived from structured, event-driven social media discussions. By explicitly modeling the interaction structure (e.g., reply density, network effects), quant strategies can potentially capture faster propagation dynamics or stronger collective opinion shifts that standard, aggregated sentiment metrics miss. This is particularly relevant for event-driven trading, volatility forecasting, or predicting short-term mispricing caused by concentrated social media narratives.
title_cn: SURGE：一个具有交互结构的事件中心社交媒体情绪时间序列基准
summary_cn: SURGE提供了一个新的基准数据集，用于分析事件驱动的社交媒体讨论的时间序列动态。它保留了帖子间的交互结构，这对量化交易具有重要意义。通过利用这些结构化情绪数据，可以开发更精细的Alpha因子，特别是用于捕捉事件发生期间市场情绪的快速演变和群体效应，从而指导事件驱动或高频交易策略。

title: Scalable On-Policy Reinforcement Learning via Adaptive Batch Scaling
summary: Conventional wisdom holds that large-batch training is fundamentally incompatible with Reinforcement Learning (RL) - beyond a modest threshold, increasing batch sizes typically yields diminishing returns or performance degradation due to the inherent non-stationarity of the data distribution. We challenge this view by observing that non-stationarity is not a fixed property of RL, but evolves throughout training: early stages exhibit rapid behavioral shifts that demand small batches for plasticity, whereas late stages approach a quasi-stationary regime where large batches enable precise convergence. Motivated by this observation, we propose Adaptive Batch Scaling (ABS), that dynamically adjusts the effective batch size according to the stability of the learning policy. Central to ABS is Behavioral Divergence, a novel metric that quantifies policy non-stationarity by measuring action-level shifts between consecutive updates, which we use to scale batch size inversely to policy volatility. Integrated with the Parallelised Q-Network (PQN) algorithm and evaluated on the ALE benchmark, ABS seamlessly reconciles early-stage plasticity with late-stage stable convergence. Strikingly, contrary to conventional wisdom, our results reveal that the combination of larger networks and larger batch sizes achieves the best performance - a scaling behavior previously thought to be unattainable in RL, now unlocked through adaptive batch control.
core_methodology: The core methodology is Adaptive Batch Scaling (ABS), a technique designed to optimize On-Policy Reinforcement Learning (RL) by dynamically adjusting the batch size during training. It uses a novel metric called Behavioral Divergence to quantify policy non-stationarity (action-level shifts between updates) and scales the batch size inversely to policy volatility. This is integrated with the Parallelised Q-Network (PQN) algorithm.
data_sources: The paper primarily uses the ALE (Arcade Learning Environment) benchmark for evaluation, which is standard for testing RL algorithms. For direct financial application, this paradigm would need to be applied to sequential financial data, such as high-frequency market orders, time series of asset prices, or continuous trading environments.
alpha_potential: The potential for alpha lies in the enhanced performance and stability of RL agents trained using ABS. In finance, RL is used for complex tasks like optimal execution, high-frequency market making, and dynamic portfolio management. ABS addresses a critical limitation in RL training (the trade-off between plasticity for exploration and stability for convergence). By allowing RL agents to learn faster and converge more robustly in non-stationary financial environments, ABS could yield superior trading policies compared to fixed-batch size methods.
title_cn: 通过自适应批次缩放实现可扩展的在线策略强化学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种自适应批次缩放（ABS）方法，动态调整强化学习（RL）中的批次大小，以解决训练初期高波动性和后期收敛需求之间的矛盾。ABS通过衡量策略不稳定性来优化RL训练，有望显著提高复杂金融环境（如最优执行或动态投资组合管理）中RL交易代理的稳定性和最终表现。

title: A Rigorous, Tractable Measure of Model Complexity
summary: An accurate assessment of a model's complexity is crucial for topics such as interpretation, generalization, and model selection. However, most existing complexity measures either rely on heuristic assumptions or are computationally prohibitive. In this paper, we present a mathematically rigorous yet easy-to-compute measure of model complexity that is based on the similarities between the model gradients across inputs. It is thus well-defined for any parametric model, but also for kernel-based non-parametric models. We prove that our measure of complexity generalizes model-specific complexity measures such as polynomial degree (for polynomial regression), kernel length scale (for Matérn kernels), number of neighbors (for k-nearest neighbors), number of splits (for decision trees), and number of trees (for random forests). We also use our measure to obtain new insights into the double descent phenomenon for random Fourier features, random forests, neural networks, and gradient boosting.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a new, mathematically rigorous, and computationally tractable measure of model complexity based on the similarity of model gradients across different inputs. This measure generalizes standard complexity metrics for various parametric and non-parametric models, including those used in deep learning and ensemble methods.
data_sources: The methodology itself is model-agnostic and depends only on the model's architecture and the input data used for training/evaluation, which in finance would typically be time-series data, cross-sectional equity/asset features, or market order book data.
alpha_potential: The direct application is improving model selection, regularization, and generalization in quantitative trading models. By providing a robust complexity measure, quants can optimize the bias-variance tradeoff more effectively than relying solely on heuristic regularization terms (like L1/L2) or simple cross-validation. This is particularly useful for complex models like deep neural networks or gradient boosting machines used for predicting asset returns or order book dynamics, potentially leading to more robust, generalizable alpha signals and better risk management by avoiding overfitting.
title_cn: 模型复杂度的严格且可处理的度量
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种基于模型梯度相似性的严格且易于计算的模型复杂度度量方法。在量化交易中，此方法可用于优化复杂模型的选择和正则化，有效平衡模型的偏差与方差，从而提升预测模型的泛化能力和信号的稳定性，减少过度拟合风险。

title: Efficient Learning of Deep State Space Models via Importance Smoothing
summary: Latent state space systems are ubiquitous in statistical modelling, arising naturally when a time series is observed through a noisy measurement function, however training deep state space models (DSSM) at scale remains difficult. Two largely distinct strategies and literatures have developed around the training of DSSMs. Firstly, auto-encoding DSSMs train generative DSSMs by optimising a variational lower bound. Secondly, DSSMs trained by back-propagating the outputs of a classical sequential Monte Carlo algorithm (SMC). Such approaches can train DSSMs for discriminative as well as generative tasks, however, due to the sequentiality of their forward pass, scale poorly on modern hardware. We propose a new training method \emph{parallel variational Monte Carlo} (PVMC) that bridges the gap between the paradigms, and can be used robustly to train DSSMs for both discriminative and generative tasks. Our method achieves state-of-the-art or better results on a set of baseline experiments and trains $10\times$ faster than the fastest competing SMC approach.
core_methodology: The core contribution is the 'Parallel Variational Monte Carlo' (PVMC) method for training Deep State Space Models (DSSMs). This method bridges the gap between variational auto-encoding approaches and Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) based training. Its key advantage is superior scalability, training significantly faster (10x faster than SMC) while maintaining high performance for both discriminative and generative tasks.
data_sources: The abstract focuses on modeling sequential data, implying its applicability to standard time series data such as high-frequency trading data, asset price series, or macroeconomic indicators.
alpha_potential: DSSMs are powerful tools for modeling dynamic, latent factors influencing noisy observations. In finance, this directly translates to superior modeling of unobserved market states (e.g., latent volatility regimes, hidden liquidity conditions, or complex factor dynamics). The efficiency gains (10x speedup) provided by PVMC make training complex, high-dimensional DSSMs tractable for real-time or high-frequency trading applications where computational speed is critical for state estimation and subsequent decision-making (e.g., in Reinforcement Learning agents or complex prediction systems).
title_cn: 基于重要性平滑的高效深度状态空间模型学习
summary_cn: 本文提出并行变分蒙特卡洛(PVMC)方法，解决了深度状态空间模型(DSSM)训练的效率和扩展性问题。该方法将生成式和判别式训练范式结合，训练速度比现有SMC方法快10倍。这使得在处理高频金融时间序列和估计隐藏市场状态（如流动性或波动性）时，可以部署更复杂、更强大的动态模型，直接提升量化策略的状态估计精度和实时性要求。

title: Expectation Consistency Loss: Rethink Confidence Calibration under Covariate Shift
summary: Confidence calibration for classification models is vital in safety-critical decision-making scenarios and has received extensive attention. General confidence calibration methods assume training and test data are independent and identically distributed, limiting their effectiveness under covariate shifts. Previous calibration methods under covariate shift struggle with class-wise or canonical calibrations and often rely on unstable importance weighting when density ratios are large or unbounded. Given the above limitations, this paper rethinks confidence calibration under covariate shifts. First, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for confidence calibration under covariate shifts, named Expectation consistency condition, which reveals covariate shifts do not necessarily lead to uncalibrated confidence and provides a weaker condition for confidence calibration than global covariate distribution alignment. Then, utilizing Expectation consistency condition, this paper proposes an unsupervised domain adaptation loss to calibrate confidence of the target domain, named Expectation consistency loss (ECL), which is compatible with canonical calibration, class-wise calibration, and top-label calibration. Third, we prove that computing ECL loss has the same sample complexity as Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and provide a theoretically grounded mini-batch trainable scheme for ECL loss. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of our method on both simulated and real-world covariate shift datasets.
core_methodology: The core methodology proposes the Expectation Consistency Loss (ECL) for unsupervised domain adaptation, specifically targeting confidence calibration in classification models facing covariate shifts. It derives a necessary and sufficient 'Expectation consistency condition' for calibration and utilizes this condition to create a trainable loss function that is compatible with various calibration types (canonical, class-wise, top-label).
data_sources: The paper validates its method on simulated and real-world datasets exhibiting covariate shifts, which, in a trading context, would correspond to using historical labeled data (training set) and applying it to new, shifted market regimes (test/target set, e.g., applying a model trained on pre-2020 bull market data to a high-volatility post-COVID regime).
alpha_potential: The primary alpha potential lies in improving the robustness and reliability of predictive models in dynamic financial markets. Financial data is notorious for regime shifts (covariate shifts). By ensuring that the model's confidence scores remain well-calibrated even when market dynamics change (e.g., transitions from low to high volatility, or structural breaks), trading systems can make much more reliable decisions regarding trade sizing, risk management, and stop-loss placements. If a model is poorly calibrated under a new regime, it might be overconfident when it should be cautious, leading to large losses. ECL offers a direct mechanism to adapt and trust model predictions during structural changes.
title_cn: 期望一致性损失：在协变量漂移下重新审视置信度校准
summary_cn: 该研究为解决金融市场中常见的协变量漂移（市场结构变化）导致的AI模型置信度失真问题，提出了期望一致性损失（ECL）。ECL是一种无监督域适应损失函数，能确保模型预测的置信度在市场状态变化时保持准确校准。这对于构建在不同市场环境下（如牛市转熊市）依然可靠的量化交易策略和风险管理至关重要，能显著提升策略的稳健性。

title: Conditioning Gaussian Processes on Almost Anything
summary: Gaussian processes (GPs) offer a principled probabilistic model over functions, but exact inference is restricted to the linear-Gaussian regime. We establish an explicit equivalence between GPs and a class of linear diffusion models, recasting predictive sampling as an ODE with closed-form Gaussian dynamics and a likelihood-dependent guidance term that admits a simple Monte Carlo approximation. In the linear-Gaussian setting, we recover standard GP conditioning exactly; beyond conjugacy, the same machinery handles any conditioning statement admitting point-wise likelihood evaluation -- including non-linear physics, and, for the first time, natural language via large language models. Whitening isolates the irreducible non-Gaussian dynamics, minimising Wasserstein-2 transport cost and eliminating numerical stiffness. The result is a general-purpose GP inference scheme requiring no bespoke derivations. Together, these results provide a general mechanism for incorporating the full richness of real-world knowledge as conditioning information, opening a new frontier for the probabilistic modelling of real-world problems.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a generalized Gaussian Process (GP) inference scheme by establishing an equivalence between GPs and linear diffusion models. This approach recasts GP prediction as solving an Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) involving Gaussian dynamics and a likelihood-dependent guidance term. Crucially, it allows for incorporating complex conditioning information (including non-linear physics and natural language via LLMs) into the GP framework without requiring bespoke derivations for each conditioning type, using Monte Carlo approximations for non-Gaussian likelihoods.
data_sources: The methodology is general, but the unique value lies in integrating non-traditional data types—specifically structured knowledge from Large Language Models (LLMs) (e.g., sentiment, thematic information, expert opinion) — as conditioning statements alongside traditional time-series data.
alpha_potential: This methodology offers significant potential for complex signal fusion. By formally integrating qualitative or high-dimensional information (like market narrative derived from LLMs) directly into a rigorous probabilistic forecasting model (GPs), quantitative strategies can move beyond simple linear factor models. This could enhance predictive power in areas historically difficult to model, such as regime detection, thematic investment alignment, or incorporating instantaneous expert views into risk models. It provides a unified probabilistic framework for combining structured quantitative inputs with unstructured qualitative inputs.
title_cn: 对几乎任何事物的条件化高斯过程
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种通用的高斯过程（GP）推理新方法，将其等效于扩散模型，并通过ODE求解。其核心价值在于首次允许将来自大型语言模型（LLMs）的自然语言信息作为条件信息纳入GP预测。这为量化策略融合高质量的定性（如市场叙事）和定量数据提供了一个统一的、可扩展的概率框架，有望提升复杂信号融合和市场预测的精度。

title: Discovering Entity-Conditioned Lag Heterogeneity: A Lag-Gated Neural Audit Framework for Panel Time Series
summary: Country-level temporal panels are widely used in empirical analysis. Researchers often need to audit how different entities respond to historical signals over different time horizons. Current approaches typically do not provide directly auditable entity-specific lag summaries. We formulate entity-conditioned heterogeneous lag discovery as a temporal panel mining task and propose AC-GATE, an Adaptive-Conditioning Encoder with a Scale-Invariant Lag Gate. It instantiates conditional Moderated Distributed Lag by using observable entity-level proxies to condition lag-weight distributions over historical observations, thereby making effective lags structural outputs of the model rather than post-hoc explanations. The evaluation is based on a layered audit protocol that separates predictive calibration from lag discovery. A synthetic panel with known ground-truth lags is used for mechanism recovery testing, and two real-world country-level panels are used for external audit and stress testing. The results show that AC-GATE can recover heterogeneous lag structure in synthetic data, and generates non-degenerate, externally structured effective lags in real data.
core_methodology: The paper introduces AC-GATE (Adaptive-Conditioning Encoder with a Scale-Invariant Lag Gate) to model entity-specific, heterogeneous lag structures in temporal panel data. It uses observable entity-level proxies to condition the distribution of lag weights, effectively creating structural outputs for effective lags rather than relying on post-hoc interpretation.
data_sources: Temporal panel data, specifically country-level economic indicators (empirical analysis) and synthetic financial panels for testing.
alpha_potential: This method provides a high-resolution, entity-specific view of how different assets (or entities in the panel, analogous to cross-sectional asset classes or securities) respond to past information over various time horizons. In finance, this is crucial for building sophisticated momentum, mean-reversion, or leading indicator strategies where the optimal lookback window (lag) is heterogeneous across different instruments or market regimes. The ability to 'audit' effective lags for each entity directly translates to adaptive signal construction and improved factor timing.
title_cn: 发现实体条件滞后异质性：一种用于面板时间序列的滞后门控神经审计框架
summary_cn: 该模型AC-GATE旨在解决面板数据中不同实体（如不同资产）对历史信息响应时间窗（滞后）的异质性问题。它通过学习并结构化输出每个实体的有效滞后信息，这对于构建适应性动量、因子时序或截面轮动的策略至关重要。该方法能更精准地捕捉跨资产的动态依赖关系，提高信号的有效性和鲁棒性。

title: NeighborDiv: Training-free Zero-shot Generalist Graph Anomaly Detection via Neighbor Diversity
summary: Graph Anomaly Detection (GAD) is increasingly shifting to Generalist GAD (GGAD) for cross-domain "one-for-all" detection, but existing GGAD methods predominantly rely on the neighbor consistency principle, falling into the \textbf{Node-to-Neighbor Consistency Paradigm} for anomaly quantification. These methods suffer from complex training pipelines, heavy training data dependency, high computational costs, and unstable cross-domain generalization. To address these limitations, we propose NeighborDiv, a training-free generalist graph anomaly detection framework based on neighbor diversity. Departing from the dominant Node-to-Neighbor Consistency Paradigm, we shift the focus to the \textbf{Neighbor-to-Neighbor Diversity Paradigm}, and uncover that the internal structural dispersion of a node's neighbor set is a powerful, independently discriminative anomaly signal. We quantify neighbor diversity via the variance of inter-neighbor feature similarities, which captures how a node organizes its local graph environment, and operates independently of conventional node-to-neighbor consistency frameworks. Extensive experiments under two standard GGAD evaluation paradigms show NeighborDiv achieves state-of-the-art performance, with relative gains of 10.25% in average AUC and 17.78% in average AP over the second-best baseline under Single-Domain Independent Training (SDIT), and 6.89%/9.58% in AUC/AP under Unified Multi-Domain Training (UMDT), respectively. Notably, NeighborDiv yields zero performance volatility across all datasets, eliminating training-set dependency and establishing a lightweight and highly practical GGAD framework.
core_methodology: The paper introduces NeighborDiv, a training-free, zero-shot framework for Graph Anomaly Detection (GAD) that pivots from the conventional 'Node-to-Neighbor Consistency Paradigm' to a 'Neighbor-to-Neighbor Diversity Paradigm.' It quantifies anomalies by measuring the diversity (variance of inter-neighbor feature similarities) within a node's immediate neighborhood, suggesting that structural dispersion in local graph environments is a significant, independent signal for identifying anomalies.
data_sources: The method is designed for general graph data structures. In a financial context, this would apply to data represented as graphs, such as inter-firm transaction networks, supply chains, complex security ownership structures, or market microstructure data where relationships (edges) between entities (nodes) are critical.
alpha_potential: The core concept of identifying anomalies via neighbor diversity has strong potential in detecting sudden, non-standard structural changes within financial networks. This could be used for early fraud detection (e.g., unusual transaction patterns in a payment network), identifying market manipulation (e.g., a stock exhibiting atypical neighborhood correlation structure relative to its peers), or flagging high-risk counterparty exposures in a portfolio where traditional metrics might fail. Since it is training-free, it offers rapid, real-time anomaly detection.
title_cn: NeighborDiv：基于邻居多样性的无训练零样本通才图异常检测
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种无需训练的图异常检测方法NeighborDiv，通过分析节点邻居特征相似度的多样性来识别异常结构。在金融领域，该方法可用于实时检测网络中的异常结构变化，例如欺诈交易模式或供应链风险，提供了一种快速且免训练的异常信号源。

title: Declarative Data Services: Structured Agentic Discovery for Composing Data Systems
summary: Agentic discovery has shown that LLM-driven search can find novel algorithms, designs, and code under benchmark conditions. Translating the paradigm to multi-system data backends surfaces a harder problem: the search space is heterogeneous, the verifier is whether a deployed stack actually runs, and composition knowledge is unevenly captured in pretraining. Unbounded agentic discovery, a coding agent iterating on failure-log feedback, fails to converge consistently on a working stack even when iteration and explicit composition knowledge are added. We propose Declarative Data Services (DDS), an architecture for structured agentic discovery of data-system compositions from declarative user intent. The framework owns four typed contracts at successive layers (intent, operator DAG, per-system skills, runtime attribution) that decompose the global search into bounded sub-searches; sub-agents search each typed space, while the framework provides the channels by which knowledge flows forward as inline skill citations and errors route backward as typed signals. As a proof of life on a trading-backend workload, DDS converges where unbounded discovery does not; runtime failures become skill patches that the next deployment cites inline. We position this as an early prototype reporting lessons from real-world data-system composition.
core_methodology: The paper introduces 'Declarative Data Services (DDS),' an architecture for structured agentic discovery, using typed contracts and bounded sub-searches to compose complex data systems reliably. It specifically addresses the failure of unbounded LLM agents to converge on working system stacks by structuring the search space and managing feedback loops (failure logs becoming skill patches). This is demonstrated on a trading-backend workload.
data_sources: The primary focus is on composing and managing the underlying data infrastructure required to run trading workloads, rather than generating alpha directly from market data. It references 'runtime attribution' and utilizes failure logs generated by the execution environment.
alpha_potential: While DDS is an infrastructure tool, achieving high-speed, reliable, and adaptive data pipelines is crucial for executing modern quantitative strategies (especially microstructure and high-frequency trading). DDS's ability to quickly self-heal and modify the data stack based on runtime errors could significantly reduce deployment latency and increase the robustness of complex, multi-stage quantitative systems, providing an operational edge.
title_cn: 声明式数据服务：用于组合数据系统的结构化智能体发现
summary_cn: 该研究提出一种名为DDS的架构，利用结构化的智能体发现机制，解决了在复杂数据后端构建和部署交易系统时的收敛性问题。通过将搜索空间分块并使失败日志成为可学习的技能补丁，DDS能更可靠地自动化构建和维护底层数据处理栈，从而提高量化策略系统部署的效率和健壮性，特别有利于依赖复杂数据管道的策略。

title: Beyond Semantic Similarity: A Two-Phase Non-Parametric Retrieval Workflow for Corporate Credit Underwriting
summary:
Corporate credit underwriting requires analysts to extract actionable evidence from long, heterogeneous financial documents spanning hundreds of pages and multiple languages. Standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines optimize for semantic similarity, which frequently surfaces passages that are topically related but lack decision utility, a problem we term the similarity-utility gap. We propose a two-phase non-parametric retrieval architecture that separates high-recall candidate retrieval from high-precision utility ranking. The first phase combines lexical and dense multilingual retrieval to construct a broad candidate pool. The second phase applies an adaptive retrieval controller that filters candidates using query intent and document structure signals, followed by an LLM-as-a-Judge utility scoring mechanism that ranks passages by analytical usefulness rather than semantic proximity.
  A context-aware extraction module preserves structural fidelity across narrative text and complex financial tables. The system is deployed entirely on-premise to satisfy enterprise data governance requirements. Evaluated on a multilingual corpus of proprietary financial documents with analyst-curated relevance labels, the system significantly outperforms naive retrieval baselines. In production deployment across more than 800 credit analysts, document review time was reduced from several hours to approximately three minutes, demonstrating the practical value of utility-aware RAG architectures for document-intensive decision-support workflows.
core_methodology: A two-phase non-parametric retrieval architecture replacing standard RAG. Phase 1 uses combined lexical and dense multilingual retrieval for high recall candidate pooling. Phase 2 employs an adaptive controller guided by query intent and document structure signals, coupled with an LLM-as-a-Judge for utility ranking, prioritizing analytical usefulness over pure semantic similarity.
data_sources: Long, heterogeneous, multilingual corporate financial documents (e.g., filings, reports, unstructured text, and financial tables).
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on credit underwriting efficiency (reducing manual review time), the core innovation—utility-aware retrieval that accurately extracts decision-relevant information from complex documents—has direct implications for trading signal generation. It can be adapted to rapidly consolidate investment theses, parse unstructured news/filings for true factor signals (ESG, governance risks, qualitative insights), drastically speeding up the research cycle for fundamental or quantitative long/short strategies. The ability to reliably extract structured data from complex tables is key.
title_cn: 超越语义相似性：企业信用承保的两阶段非参数检索工作流程
summary_cn: 该研究提出一种双阶段的非参数RAG架构，用于解决传统语义检索在金融文档中存在的“相似性-效用间隙”。系统通过结合多语言检索和基于效用的LLM裁判机制，高效地从复杂、非结构化的财务文件中提取具有决策价值的信息。该技术可显著加速量化研究员和基金经理对海量企业报告、新闻的分析速度，从而加速新因子/信号的发现与验证。

title: LT2: Linear-Time Looped Transformers
summary: Looped Transformers (LT) have emerged as a powerful architecture by iterating their layers multiple times before decoding the final token. However, pairing them with full attention retains quadratic complexity, making them computationally expensive and slow. We introduce LT2 (Linear-Time Looped Transformers), a family of looped architectures that replace quadratic softmax attention with subquadratic, linear-time attention. We study two variants: LT2-linear with linear attention and LT2-sparse with sparse attention. We find that looping uniquely synergizes with these variants: it enables iterative memory refinement in linear attention and progressively expands the effective receptive field in sparse attention. We formalize these benefits theoretically and demonstrate consistent empirical gains across controlled recall, state-tracking, and language modeling tasks. We then explore LT2-hybrid, which combines different attention variants in a looped setting. Two variants are especially promising: LT2-hybrid (GDN+DSA), which interleaves linear and sparse attention to maximize efficiency and matches the standard looped transformer's quality at fully linear-time cost; and LT2-hybrid (Full+GDN), which interleaves GDN with a small fraction of full attention layers to maximize quality, surpassing the standard looped transformer in both performance and efficiency. We also show how to convert a pre-trained LT into an LT2-hybrid model. With about 1B tokens of training, our converted model, Ouro-hybrid-1.4B, outperforms industry-level 1B models and is competitive with industry-level 4B models while retaining the speed benefits of linear-time attention. Together, these results show a clear path toward making looped transformers more scalable and advancing efficient, capable small language models.
core_methodology: The paper introduces LT2 (Linear-Time Looped Transformers), an evolution of Looped Transformers designed for computational efficiency. It replaces the standard quadratic-complexity full attention mechanism with linear-time attention variants (LT2-linear, LT2-sparse) or hybrid models that interleave different attention types (e.g., LT2-hybrid (GDN+DSA), LT2-hybrid (Full+GDN)). The key innovation is achieving near full-attention quality with linear time complexity by leveraging iterative memory refinement through looping.
data_sources: The paper focuses on general NLP benchmarks (recall, state-tracking, language modeling), not specifically financial data. However, the architecture is designed to handle sequential data, which can be directly applied to time-series financial data (e.g., high-frequency tick data, price sequences, market state vectors).
alpha_potential: The architecture's primary value is enabling the training and deployment of very large, efficient sequence models using linear-time attention. In finance, this translates to creating custom LLMs or sequence models capable of processing long sequences of market data (order book snapshots, news narratives, market history) much faster and cheaper than quadratic models. This efficiency allows for developing highly complex, context-aware predictive models for tasks like market microstructure analysis, high-frequency trading signals, or complex temporal factor modeling where speed and sequence length matter.
title_cn: 线性时间循环Transformer架构 (LT2)
summary_cn: 该研究提出LT2架构，通过引入线性时间和稀疏注意力机制，将循环Transformer的计算复杂度从二次降为线性。这使得金融领域在处理长序列价格数据、订单流和市场状态时，能更快、更经济地部署高性能的预测模型，有望提升高频交易和复杂因子模型的效率与表现。

title: Continuous Timing Signals for Growth-Defensive Style Allocation: Factor Attribution, Risk Matching, and Out-of-Sample Evidence
summary:
This paper studies conditional allocation between a growth/technology ETF basket, denoted by $G$, and a defensive income/value-oriented ETF basket, denoted by $D$.
