Existing memory benchmarks predominantly evaluate retention of personalized information in multi-turn chat scenarios, overlooking the dynamic memory formation that occurs during extended agent execution. Consequently, the memory systems they produce transfer poorly to realistic agentic environments, such as coding and web navigation. We present MemGym, a benchmark for agentic memory that unifies existing agent gyms and in-house memory-grounded pipelines behind one memory-reasoning interface. MemGym spans five evaluation tracks grouped into four agentic regimes: tool-use dialogue (tau2-bench), multi-turn deep-research search (MEMGYM-DR), coding (SWE-Gym and MEMGYM-CODEQA), and computer use (WebArena-Infinity). MemGym reports memory-isolated scores that decouple memory performance from reasoning, retrieval, and tool-use ability, so memory strategies can be ranked without those confounders. Our synthetic pipelines for MEMGYM-CODEQA and MEMGYM-DR are length-controllable, ablation-verified at every stage, and tightly aligned with downstream scenarios. To make evaluation on coding environments academically tractable, we train MemRM, a lightweight reward model (Qwen3-1.7B fine-tuned with QLoRA) that scores compression quality as a fast scalar read in place of full Docker rollouts.
core_methodology: The paper introduces MemGym, a standardized benchmark environment designed to evaluate the long-horizon memory capabilities of Large Language Model (LLM) agents across various complex tasks (coding, web navigation, multi-turn research). It focuses on isolating memory performance from reasoning and tool-use abilities through controlled evaluation tracks and length-controllable synthetic data pipelines. It also includes MemRM, a lightweight reward model used to score memory retention in complex code execution environments.
data_sources: The paper uses synthetic agentic environments like tool-use dialogue benchmarks (tau2-bench), multi-turn deep research scenarios (MEMGYM-DR), coding platforms (SWE-Gym, MEMGYM-CODEQA), and web interaction environments (WebArena-Infinity). These are not traditional financial market data but rather task/simulation environments designed to test agentic capabilities.
alpha_potential: While MemGym itself is a benchmark for general agentic capabilities (not directly financial data), the core mechanism—developing robust, long-horizon memory systems for autonomous agents—is highly relevant. Successful long-horizon memory in LLM agents could enable complex, persistent trading strategies that require synthesizing information over extended market observation periods (e.g., tracking evolving macroeconomic narratives, complex regulatory changes, or multi-stage arbitrage setups that span weeks or months). The ability to decouple memory performance from reasoning is crucial for cleanly optimizing memory architecture for high-stakes financial analysis.
title_cn: MemGym：一个用于LLM智能体的长周期记忆环境
summary_cn: 该研究提出了MemGym基准，用于评估LLM智能体在需要长期记忆的复杂任务中的能力。虽然环境本身非金融数据，但其核心的、解耦的记忆评估方法对开发需要长期信息整合和一致性推理的复杂量化交易智能体具有重要借鉴意义。提升智能体的持久记忆能力是实现持续、复杂策略自动化的关键。

title: Assessing socio-economic climate impacts from text data
summary: Recent advances in natural language processing (NLP) and large language models (LLMs) have enabled the systematic use of large-scale textual data from news, social media, and reports to create datasets with socio-economic impacts of climate hazards such as floods, droughts, storms, and multi-hazard events. As the field of text-as-data for impact assessment expands, so does its methodological complexity. Yet research remains fragmented, with no clear guidelines for defining what constitutes an impact, handling temporal and spatial biases, and selecting appropriate modeling and post-processing strategies. This lack of coherence limits transparency and comparability across studies. Here, we address this gap by synthesising common practices, describing key challenges specific to the use of text-as-data methods for analyzing socio-economic impact data, and proposing recommendations to address them. By providing guidance on best practices, we aim to support the construction of robust text-derived socio-economic impact datasets that can more accurately inform disaster risk management and attribution studies.
core_methodology: The paper focuses on synthesizing best practices, defining methodologies, and establishing guidelines for extracting socio-economic impact assessments (e.g., quantifying flood/drought impacts) from large-scale textual data (news, social media, reports) using NLP and LLMs. The methods emphasized involve defining impact, handling biases (temporal/spatial), and choosing appropriate modeling/post-processing techniques.
data_sources: Large-scale textual data from news articles, social media feeds, and official disaster/climate reports related to natural hazards (floods, droughts, storms).
alpha_potential: While the paper is framed around disaster risk management, the core methodology—systematically quantifying climate-hazard impacts from text data using LLMs—is highly relevant for finance. Alpha can be generated by using these derived socio-economic impact scores as novel, high-frequency alternative data signals. Specifically, these signals can predict supply chain disruptions, commodity price volatility, regional economic shifts, or insurance/reinsurance exposure, providing an edge in macro overlays or sector-specific trading strategies well ahead of traditional financial reporting that incorporates these events.
title_cn: 从文本数据评估气候变化的社会经济影响
summary_cn: 该研究提供构建健壮文本派生社会经济影响数据集的最佳实践指南。在量化交易中，这些方法可用于实时解析全球新闻和社交媒体，量化特定气候事件（如干旱、洪水）对区域经济和供应链的冲击程度。这些高频、前瞻性的冲击指标可作为构建宏观对冲或特定行业（如农业、保险、能源）因子和Alpha信号的独特另类数据源。

title: Cumulative Meta-Learning from Active Learning Queries for Robustness to Spurious Correlations
summary: Spurious correlations in real-world datasets cause machine learning models to rely on irrelevant patterns, undermining reliability, generalization, and fairness. Active learning offers a promising way to address this failure mode by querying informative samples that distinguish core features from spurious ones. However, standard active-learning methods simply append queried examples to the labeled set, effectively updating only the likelihood term. In deep learning regimes, the influence of these informative samples can be diluted by the larger labeled set and memorized by overparameterized models. We propose Cumulative Active Meta-Learning (CAML), an active-learning framework that uses queried examples to meta-learn the prior, or inductive bias, governing how the model adapts. CAML casts each active-learning round as a meta-learning task: the current labeled set serves as meta-train data for adaptation, while the newly queried batch serves as meta-test data for evaluating generalization. Unlike conventional meta-learning, which treats tasks as independent and identically distributed, CAML exploits the sequential dependence between active-learning rounds by maintaining a cumulative inductive bias that is progressively refined. Theoretically, we show that this cumulative formulation introduces interaction terms that couple earlier meta-learned inductive biases with later query-induced objectives, capturing dependencies absent from standard meta-learning. Empirically, CAML improves minority-group accuracy across spurious-correlation benchmarks and acquisition strategies, with gains of up to 27.8% on Dominoes, 29.9% on Waterbirds, 14.3% on SpuCo, and 24.0% on CivilComments.
core_methodology: The core methodology is Cumulative Active Meta-Learning (CAML), a framework designed to improve model robustness against spurious correlations. It structures active learning rounds as sequential meta-learning tasks, where the model meta-learns a cumulative inductive bias that adapts based on newly queried informative samples. This refines the prior distribution over model parameters.
data_sources: The paper uses benchmark datasets for evaluating spurious correlations (e.g., Dominoes, Waterbirds, SpuCo, CivilComments). In a financial context, this approach would require structured, labeled datasets where true signals might be confounded by irrelevant patterns (spurious correlations), such as historical time series data where market regimes shift unexpectedly or indicator relationships break down.
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on improving general robustness against spurious correlations (often encountered in vision/NLP benchmarks), the methodology is highly relevant for financial time series forecasting. Financial markets are notoriously prone to regime shifts and spurious correlations (e.g., indicators that work well in bull markets failing in bear markets). CAML's ability to progressively learn an inductive bias that filters out irrelevant patterns (spurious signals) via targeted data selection (active querying) offers a pathway to building more robust predictive and decision-making models (e.g., for classification or regression tasks within a trading signal generator). Success relies on defining informative queries in a financial context.
title_cn: 用于鲁棒性应对虚假相关性的累积主动元学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出累积主动元学习（CAML）框架，通过序列化地元学习和迭代优化模型归纳偏置，有效应对数据中的虚假相关性。在量化交易中，此方法可用于构建对市场结构变化（如牛熊转换）或无效因子（噪音信号）具有更强鲁棒性的预测模型，从而提升策略的长期稳定性。

title: Conflict-Aware Additive Guidance for Flow Models under Compositional Rewards
summary: Inference-time guided sampling steers state-of-the-art diffusion and flow models without fine-tuning by interpreting the generation process as a controllable trajectory. This provides a simple and flexible way to inject external constraints (e.g., cost functions or pre-trained verifiers) for controlled generation. However, existing methods often fail when composing multiple constraints simultaneously, which leads to deviations from the true data manifold. In this work, we identify root causes of this off-manifold drift and find that the approximation error scales severely with gradient misalignment. Building on these findings, we propose Conflict-Aware Additive Guidance ($g^\text{car}$), a lightweight and learnable method, which actively rectifies off-manifold drift by dynamically detecting and resolving gradient conflicts. We validate $g^\text{car}$ across diverse domains, ranging from synthetic datasets and image editing to generative decision-making for planning and control. Our results demonstrate that $g^\text{car}$ effectively rectifies off-manifold drift, surpassing baselines in generation fidelity while using light compute. Code is available at https://github.com/yuxuehui/CAR-guidance.
core_methodology: The core methodology introduces Conflict-Aware Additive Guidance ($g^{\text{car}}$) for flow models (e.g., diffusion models) during inference. This method dynamically detects and resolves gradient conflicts arising from combining multiple guiding constraints, thereby rectifying 'off-manifold drift' and improving generation fidelity under complex guidance conditions.
data_sources: The paper focuses on synthetic datasets, image editing, and general generative decision-making/control problems. It does not directly use financial market data, but the underlying generative modeling techniques are generalizable.
alpha_potential: The potential in quantitative finance lies in using advanced generative models (like flow models or diffusion models) for complex tasks such as synthetic data generation (e.g., simulating market paths under specific regimes), generating counterfactual scenarios for risk management, or creating structured synthetic market data for training robust agents/classifiers. The ability to handle and combine multiple constraints (e.g., incorporating technical constraints alongside learned features) without degradation is valuable for refining complex financial simulations or generating highly specific trading signals/scenarios.
title_cn: 面向组合奖励下冲突感知的加性指导方法
summary_cn: 该研究提出一种轻量级的冲突感知加性指导方法 ($g^{\text{car}}$)，用于改进受控生成模型（如流模型）在同时施加多个约束时的性能。在量化交易中，这项技术可应用于在复杂约束（如风险预算、特定市场微观结构限制和模型预测输出）下生成高保真、多目标优化的合成市场数据或交易路径，从而增强策略训练和情景分析的鲁棒性。

title: Distribution-Aware Reward: Reinforcement Learning over Predictive Distributions for LLM Regression
summary: Large language models can predict real-valued quantities from heterogeneous inputs such as text, code, and molecular strings, but most training objectives score each decoded floating-point number independently, improving point estimates without ensuring calibrated predictive distributions. This limits applications requiring candidate ranking or uncertainty estimation. We introduce Distribution-Aware Reward, an on-policy reinforcement learning objective whose main contribution is to train language models to produce better predictive distributions for regression tasks, rather than only optimizing individual decoded outputs against scalar targets. Our method treats multiple decoded samples as an empirical predictive distribution, evaluates it with the Continuous Ranked Probability Score, and assigns leave-one-out credit based on each rollout's marginal contribution to distribution quality, rewarding predictions that are both accurate and appropriately dispersed. We evaluate our method on a controlled Gaussian-mixture task, code performance prediction, and molecular property prediction from SMILES strings. Across tasks, our method improves over supervised fine-tuning and pointwise reinforcement learning baselines, with strong rank-correlation gains, including a 6-point Spearman improvement on KBSS. On MoleculeNet, it uses only SMILES strings yet remains competitive with strong graph-based and 3D molecular models. Further analyses show that our method mitigates rollout diversity collapse and improves uncertainty diagnostics, suggesting that directly optimizing predictive distributions makes language model regression more robust and better calibrated.
core_methodology: The core methodology introduces 'Distribution-Aware Reward' (DAR), an on-policy Reinforcement Learning (RL) objective for training Large Language Models (LLMs) on regression tasks. Instead of optimizing for single point estimates, DAR treats multiple model rollouts as an empirical predictive distribution, evaluates it using the Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS), and assigns credit based on the marginal contribution of each rollout to the overall distribution quality. This explicitly trains the LLM to generate calibrated uncertainty estimates alongside accurate central predictions.
data_sources: The paper primarily uses synthetic data (Gaussian mixtures), code performance data, and molecular property data (SMILES strings). While not direct financial market data, the methodology is designed to handle heterogeneous inputs (text, code, strings) and output calibrated real-valued predictions.
alpha_potential: The direct application in finance is not explicitly detailed, but the breakthrough lies in generating *calibrated* probabilistic forecasts from unstructured/heterogeneous data inputs (textual news, transcripts, economic reports). For instance, an LLM trained with DAR could analyze earnings call transcripts or news sentiment and output a prediction distribution for a stock's next-day return or volatility, explicitly quantifying the uncertainty. This shift from point forecasts to calibrated distributions is critical for risk-aware portfolio construction, options pricing, and robust allocation decisions (e.g., Kelly criteria, portfolio optimization under uncertainty).
title_cn: 分布感知奖励：用于LLM回归的基于预测分布的强化学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种创新的强化学习奖励机制（DAR），旨在训练大型语言模型（LLM）在回归任务中生成具备校准不确定性的预测分布，而非仅仅优化点估计。在金融领域，此方法可用于分析文本数据（如财报、新闻）并输出具有可靠风险度量的价格或波动率预测分布。这能显著提升基于LLM的量化策略在投资组合优化和风险管理中的稳健性。

title: Everywhere Valid Bounds on False Discovery Proportions in Conformal Inference
summary: Modern applications of conformal inference to multiple testing problems, such as outlier detection and candidate selection, often involve selecting test samples whose conformal p-values fall below a threshold. The quality of such methods is often measured by the false discovery proportion (FDP), defined as the fraction of incorrect selections. Existing approaches typically control the expected value of the FDP, using methods such as the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. This approach fails to provide high-probability bounds on the realized false discovery proportion and invalidates statistical guarantees if the rejection threshold is selected after inspecting the data. This paper establishes finite-sample, distribution-free upper bounds on the FDP that hold simultaneously over all possible rejection thresholds, enabling arbitrary post hoc selection of the threshold. Simultaneous validity is achieved by constructing a high-probability envelope for the empirical distribution function of null conformal p-values by sampling from their joint distribution. Furthermore, our framework allows practitioners to modulate the envelope's shape, thereby producing tight bounds in rejection regions of primary interest. We use this flexible approach to derive simultaneous FDP upper bounds for both outlier detection and conformal selection. We demonstrate through synthetic and real-data experiments that the resulting bounds are both valid and substantially less conservative than those derived from existing approaches.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a novel framework within Conformal Inference to derive simultaneous, distribution-free, finite-sample upper bounds on the False Discovery Proportion (FDP). It achieves this by constructing a high-probability envelope for the empirical distribution function of null conformal p-values, which remains valid even after post hoc selection of the rejection threshold.
data_sources: The experimental validation uses synthetic data and real-data experiments, though the methodology itself is general and applicable to any data where hypothesis testing or multi-testing procedures (e.g., feature selection, anomaly detection) are employed, such as time series features or signal rankings.
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on statistical methodology (FDP control) rather than direct alpha generation, controlling the FDP with high probability is critical for robust algorithmic trading systems, particularly those involving large-scale feature selection, cross-asset strategy validation, or high-frequency decision making. Better control over false positives during strategy construction or signal selection leads to more reliable and less risky strategies. This methodology enhances the robustness of the 'search' process in quantitative research.
title_cn: 保形推断中对错误发现比例的普适有效边界
summary_cn: 该研究提出了保形推断的新框架，用于在多重检验中控制错误发现比例（FDP），并提供高概率保证的边界。这对于量化交易中大规模信号筛选、因子选择或异常检测至关重要。改进的FDP控制能显著提高策略选择的鲁棒性和可靠性，减少发现假阳性信号的风险。

title: Decision-Path Patterns as Tree Reliability Signals: Path-based Adaptive Weighting for Random Forest Classification
summary: Random forests aggregate trees by averaging leaf class distributions with uniform per-tree weight, which flattens local tree expertise into a globally averaged boundary. To refine this boundary locally, we look for signals in how individual trees navigate the feature space around each sample. We observe that the structural pattern of each tree's root-to-leaf decision path -- where and how often the dominant class label flips along it -- carries such a signal, conditional on the tree's final decision and the regional context where the sample lies. We propose a class-conditional ratio weighting that exploits this signal while guaranteeing zero expected class bias by construction, refining the ensemble decision near the boundary without trading one class against another. On 30 binary classification benchmarks (30 repeats), the proposed method yields a statistically significant accuracy improvement over RF (Wilcoxon p = 0.007), while weighted RF and the KNORA family do not reach significance (all p > 0.5). The gain is small (Δacc = +0.0011) but consistent across forest sizes from 100 to 1,000 trees, and regresses neither class (majority 0/30, minority 2/30) -- unlike KNORA-Eliminate, which lifts minority recall at the cost of majority regressions on 8/30 datasets.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a novel weighting scheme for Random Forests based on analyzing the root-to-leaf decision paths of individual trees. It assigns weights based on the structural pattern of how a sample traverses the feature space within each tree, specifically looking at label flips along the path. This refines local ensemble decisions near the classification boundary without introducing systemic class bias.
data_sources: The evaluation uses 30 binary classification benchmarks, which are general-purpose datasets (not explicitly finance-related in the abstract). However, the methodology is readily applicable to any time-series or cross-sectional financial classification problem (e.g., predicting stock direction, identifying regime shifts).
alpha_potential: This work addresses a core limitation in ensemble methods (uniform weighting) by introducing a finer-grained, sample-specific weighting based on local structural evidence provided by individual trees. In finance, this could lead to more robust and accurate predictions for complex, non-linear tasks like short-term directional prediction or regime classification where local decision boundaries are crucial. The consistent, albeit small, accuracy improvement suggests a methodology that could enhance the precision of existing ML-based trading signals, particularly near decision frontiers.
title_cn: 决策路径模式作为树可靠性信号：随机森林分类的基于路径的自适应加权
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种新的随机森林模型权重分配方法，该方法通过分析单个决策树从根到叶的决策路径结构来评估树的局部贡献。该技术旨在提高分类边界附近的预测精度，特别适用于金融市场中复杂的、非线性的二元分类任务（如短期方向预测或市场状态识别）。虽然提升较小，但其一致性表明了其在增强现有量化信号模型鲁棒性和准确性方面的潜力。

title: Matryoshka Concept Bottleneck Models
summary: Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) have emerged as a prominent paradigm for interpretable deep learning, learning by grounding predictions in human-understandable concepts. However, their practical deployment is hindered by the high cost of test-time intervention, as correcting model errors typically requires human experts to manually inspect and verify a large set of predicted concepts. Existing approaches suffer from a fundamental structural limitation: they either adopt a single static concept set, forcing experts to exhaustively annotate concepts and incurring prohibitive intervention costs, or train multiple models tailored to different concept budgets, resulting in substantial computational and maintenance overhead. To address this challenge, we propose the Matryoshka Concept Bottleneck Model (MCBM), a unified architecture that enables adaptive concept utilization within a single model. Inspired by Matryoshka Representation Learning, MCBM organizes concepts into a nested hierarchy based on maximum relevance and minimum redundancy, allowing inference at multiple levels of conceptual granularity without retraining. Theoretically, we show that MCBM reduces the expected intervention costs from linear to logarithmic order, $O(\log K)$, while guaranteeing monotonic performance improvement. Empirically, extensive experiments demonstrate that MCBM matches the performance of independently trained models while enabling dynamic and efficient expert interaction.
core_methodology: The core methodology introduces the Matryoshka Concept Bottleneck Model (MCBM), a novel architecture that organizes concepts in a nested hierarchy. This allows for adaptive concept utilization, enabling inference at different levels of conceptual granularity without model retraining, which drastically reduces the cost of expert intervention (from linear to logarithmic time complexity).
data_sources: The paper focuses on the methodology for interpretable deep learning, specifically concerning concept verification. While not explicitly mentioning financial data, the application would involve structured or unstructured data where human expertise is required to interpret intermediate model representations (e.g., qualitative sentiment analysis, fundamental data parsing, regulatory filing interpretation).
alpha_potential: The direct alpha potential is moderate. This is an ML interpretability and efficiency improvement, not a trading strategy itself. However, in areas of quantitative finance heavily relying on complex, interpretable models (e.g., LLM-based analysis of earnings calls, credit risk scoring based on regulatory text, or nuanced anomaly detection), MCBM could significantly speed up model debugging, calibration, and iteration. By reducing the cost of expert verification of intermediate concepts, it allows quants to deploy and refine high-stakes, interpretable models faster and more robustly, indirectly leading to better, more agile alpha capture.
title_cn: 俄罗斯套娃概念瓶颈模型
summary_cn: 该研究提出MCBM架构，通过嵌套概念层级实现自适应概念利用，无需重新训练即可动态调整概念粒度。这极大地降低了模型调试和专家干预的成本，使其在涉及复杂决策解释的量化金融应用（如LLM驱动的文本分析或高风险模型验证）中，能更高效、更稳健地部署和迭代模型，加速最终Alpha信号的捕捉与验证。

title: Adaptive RBF-KAN: A Comparative Evaluation of Dynamic Shape Parameters in Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
summary: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) approximate multivariate functions using learnable univariate edge functions, typically parameterized by B-spline bases. Although effective, spline-based implementations can be computationally expensive. A modified version of KANs, called FastKAN, improves efficiency by replacing splines with Gaussian radial basis functions (RBFs), but it relies on a fixed kernel and shape parameter. In this work, we extend the RBF-based KAN framework by introducing a broader family of radial basis kernels and by initializing the kernel shape parameter using leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study that integrates LOOCV-based kernel scale estimation with deep KAN training. We also introduce Matérn and Wendland kernels into the KAN framework for the first time, enabling more flexible basis representations beyond the Gaussian kernel used in FastKAN. The LOOCV estimate provides a data-driven initialization of the kernel scale, which is subsequently refined during network training. The proposed adaptive RBF-KAN is evaluated on several two-dimensional benchmark functions. The results highlight the importance of kernel selection and adaptive shape parameters, with different kernels showing advantages for smooth functions, discontinuities, and oscillatory patterns. Overall, combining LOOCV-based initialization with adaptive kernel learning provides a practical strategy for improving RBF-based KAN models.
core_methodology: The paper proposes Adaptive RBF-KAN, extending Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) by replacing fixed spline-based functions with radially basis functions (RBFs). It introduces adaptive kernel shape parameter initialization using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV) and integrates novel kernels (Matérn, Wendland) beyond the standard Gaussian kernel in FastKAN. This allows for data-driven optimization of the network's basis functions during training.
data_sources: Benchmark two-dimensional mathematical functions are used for evaluation, not actual financial data.
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on mathematical benchmarks, the core innovation—adaptive kernel learning using LOOCV initialization within a KAN framework—offers a highly flexible, non-linear modeling tool. In quantitative finance, KANs are being explored for complex function approximation, such as modeling non-linear relationships in asset price dynamics, volatility surfaces, or optimally pricing exotic derivatives where traditional methods struggle with high-order interactions. The adaptive nature of RBF-KAN could lead to more robust and efficient models for forecasting or portfolio construction compared to standard MLPs or even fixed-kernel RBF networks.
title_cn: 自适应RBF-KAN：动态形状参数在科尔莫果洛夫-阿诺德网络中的比较评估
summary_cn: 该研究提出了自适应RBF-KAN模型，通过使用LOOCV技术初始化和训练径向基函数的形状参数，增强了KANs的灵活性和表达能力。这项技术为金融建模提供了更强大的非线性函数逼近工具，可应用于复杂的因子挖掘、衍生品定价或构建更精确的资产回报预测模型。

title: Quadratic Characterizations for Reachability Analysis of Neural Networks
summary: Quadratic constraints (QCs) are widely used to characterize nonlinearities and uncertainties, but generic analytical characterizations can be conservative on bounded domains. This paper develops a framework for constructing verified quadratic characterizations of scalar relations in the two-dimensional real plane. Candidate quadratic inequalities are locally generated by solving convex quadratic programs using samples from the relation and exterior sample points. They are then verified globally using sum-of-squares certificates over an exact semialgebraic description or, in the case of nonpolynomial relations, over relaxed polynomial descriptions. The resulting verified constraints define a sound overapproximation of the scalar relations over the considered domains. These constraints are directly compatible with existing analysis frameworks based on QCs and pointwise integral quadratic constraints (IQCs) for static nonlinearities and uncertainties, and they can also be embedded in QC-based semidefinite programs for reachability and safety analysis of feedforward neural networks. For smooth activations such as $\tanh$, the method yields domain-dependent quadratic characterizations that constitute an alternative to generic sector- or slope-based descriptions. For ReLU networks, we give methods to reduce conservatism in QC-based reachability analysis of feedforward networks by exploiting dependencies between neurons and tighter local bounds. Numerical examples demonstrate improved reachability results for smooth activations, reduced conservatism for ReLU networks, and applicability beyond neural networks through an example involving saturation.
core_methodology: The paper develops a framework for constructing verified quadratic characterizations (Quadratic Constraints, QCs) for scalar relations, especially focusing on non-linearities in neural networks (like ReLU and smooth activations). It uses locally generated convex quadratic programs and Sum-of-Squares (SOS) certification for global verification, leading to sound overapproximations compatible with QC-based reachability and safety analysis frameworks.
data_sources: Primarily theoretical application to neural network structures (weights, biases, activation functions) derived from financial models or data. Does not explicitly deal with market time-series data, but rather the internal dynamic behavior of ML models.
alpha_potential: The primary value for quantitative trading lies in ensuring the robustness, safety, and predictability of complex deep learning models used in trading (e.g., those used for signal generation or execution optimization). By providing tighter, verifiable quadratic bounds on the behavior of ReLU and smooth activation networks, this methodology allows researchers to perform sound reachability analysis. This is crucial for building 'safe' AI agents, understanding model uncertainty bounds, and preventing catastrophic failures or unpredictable behavior in high-stakes, high-frequency environments, thereby improving the overall reliability of black-box trading systems.
title_cn: 神经网络可达性分析的二次刻画
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种为神经网络（特别是ReLU和光滑激活函数网络）的非线性行为构建精确且可验证的二次约束（QC）框架。它通过局部二次规划和SOS证明提供更紧凑的边界，减少保守性。这对于量化交易至关重要，因为它允许对深度学习交易模型的鲁棒性和安全性进行严格的数学验证，确保模型在实际市场波动中行为可控，从而提高AI驱动策略的可靠性。

title: AgentCo-op: Retrieval-Based Synthesis of Interoperable Multi-Agent Workflows
summary: Designing multi-agent workflows is especially difficult in open-ended scientific settings where tasks lack curated training sets, reliable scalar evaluation metrics, and standardized interfaces between existing tools and agents. We propose AgentCo-op, a retrieval-based synthesis framework that composes reusable skills, tools, and external agents into executable workflows through typed artifact handoffs, then applies bounded self-guided local repair to implicated components when execution evidence indicates failure. In two open-world genomics case studies, AgentCo-op composes independently developed scientific agents and external tool repositories into auditable workflows without redesigning them or running global topology search. It coordinates specialized agents for spatial transcriptomics and gene-set interpretation to enable collaborative discovery from spatial transcriptomics data, and builds a parallel workflow for cross-modality marker analysis on single-cell multiome data. AgentCo-op can also import a searched workflow as a structural prior and improve it by grounding nodes with retrieved components and applying local repair, showing that synthesis and search are complementary. On six coding, math, and question-answering benchmarks, AgentCo-op achieves the best result on four benchmarks and the best average score under a unified backbone setting, while consistently reducing per-task cost relative to multi-agent baselines. Together, these results suggest that retrieval-based synthesis can extend automated agentic workflow design beyond benchmark-optimized agent graphs to open-world workflows built from existing agents, tools, and typed artifacts.
core_methodology: AgentCo-op is a retrieval-based synthesis framework for composing reusable skills, tools, and agents into executable, interoperable workflows via typed artifact handoffs. It incorporates bounded self-guided local repair activated by execution evidence indicating failure. This methodology is fundamentally about automating complex, multi-step computational pipelines using specialized agents.
data_sources: The paper focuses on scientific data (genomics, spatial transcriptomics, single-cell multiome data) to demonstrate robustness in open-world settings, not financial market data. Adaptation requires integrating financial data sources.
alpha_potential: The direct application in finance is low, as the demonstration is in genomics. However, the *methodology* has high potential. In quantitative finance, many complex tasks (e.g., developing novel factor signals, backtesting complex strategy combinations, or executing multi-stage arbitrage/market making) require chaining together various specialized models (data cleaning, feature extraction, prediction models, optimization routines). AgentCo-op offers a systematic, verifiable way to automate the construction and maintenance of these complex, interoperable trading workflows using existing quantitative libraries (tools) and pre-trained models (agents). The local repair mechanism is crucial for maintaining robustness in evolving market conditions where models or data sources might fail.
title_cn: AgentCo-op：用于互操作性多智能体工作流的检索式合成框架
summary_cn: AgentCo-op提供了一种自动构建复杂、可互操作的交易策略工作流的框架。它通过检索和组合现有工具和模型（智能体），实现稳健的、端到端的金融数据处理和信号生成流程。其本地修复机制尤其适用于适应快速变化的市场环境，有助于提高复杂量化策略的鲁棒性和可维护性。

title: Score-Based Causal Discovery of Latent Variable Causal Models
summary: Identifying latent variables and the causal structure involving them is essential across various scientific fields. While many existing works fall under the category of constraint-based methods (with e.g. conditional independence or rank deficiency tests), they may face empirical challenges such as testing-order dependency, error propagation, and choosing an appropriate significance level. These issues can potentially be mitigated by properly designed score-based methods, such as Greedy Equivalence Search (GES) (Chickering, 2002) in the specific setting without latent variables. Yet, formulating score-based methods with latent variables is highly challenging. In this work, we develop score-based methods that are capable of identifying causal structures containing causally-related latent variables with identifiability guarantees. Specifically, we show that a properly formulated scoring function can achieve score equivalence and consistency for structure learning of latent variable causal models. We further provide a characterization of the degrees of freedom for the marginal over the observed variables under multiple structural assumptions considered in the literature, and accordingly develop both exact and continuous score-based methods. This offers a unified view of several existing constraint-based methods with different structural assumptions. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.
core_methodology: The paper proposes novel score-based methods (analogous to GES) for discovering causal structures that explicitly incorporate latent variables. It focuses on developing a robust scoring function that ensures score equivalence and consistency when latent variables are present, offering an exact or continuous approach derived from characterizing the degrees of freedom under various structural assumptions.
data_sources: The methods are designed for complex systems where observed variables are influenced by unobserved (latent) factors. In finance, this translates to using observed market data (e.g., asset returns, trading volumes) where underlying, unobserved macroeconomic, sentiment, or systemic risk factors (the latent variables) are hypothesized to drive observable correlations.
alpha_potential: This research is highly relevant for building robust causal inference models in finance, which is crucial for moving beyond mere correlation in strategy design. Identifying latent causal drivers (e.g., identifying true 'systemic risk' factors vs. observed proxies) can lead to more stable and generalizable factors. A deeper understanding of the causal architecture, especially involving latent factors, significantly enhances portfolio optimization, risk management (by correctly attributing risk sources), and constructing specialized factor rotation strategies that anticipate regime shifts driven by these unobserved causes.
title_cn: 基于分数的潜变量因果模型的潜在变量因果发现
summary_cn: 该研究开发了适用于识别包含潜在驱动因素的金融市场因果结构的新型基于分数的算法。通过精确发现隐藏的宏观经济或系统性风险因子（潜在变量）及其与可观测资产价格或流动性指标之间的因果关系，量化策略可以构建更稳健的风险模型、设计对潜在结构变化不敏感的套利/因子策略，并实现更准确的风险归因。

title: Latent Geometry as a Structural Monitor: Eigenspace Alignment for Anomaly Detection in Anonymity Networks
summary: Traditional anomaly detection marks events when measured signals cross predefined thresholds. This captures the moment of transition but not the structural pressure that precedes it. We propose treating large behavioral populations as geometric energy landscapes whose deformation can be measured before and during major transitions. The central thesis is that structure precedes geometry: the structural organization of the population is the signal, and geometric metrics are instruments for measuring it. Applied to the Tor anonymity network across 67 consecutive daily observation windows, the dual-observer pipeline identifies a stable nine-dimensional load-bearing subspace invariant across the observation period and validates this structure by Monte Carlo simulation at 16.8 sigma above the noise floor. Primary detection gates achieve 0.0% false positive rate on 24 confirmed stable windows. Forensic analysis of the February 20, 2026 confirmed infrastructure event formally falsifies the relay-departure hypothesis, identifying connectivity degradation without topology change as a detectable network failure mode. The result is a candidate structural-monitoring framework for behavioral populations with sufficient telemetry.
core_methodology: The core methodology involves treating a population's behavior (e.g., network activity, transaction patterns) as a high-dimensional geometric energy landscape. It uses Principal Component Analysis (PCA) implicitly via 'eigenspace alignment' to identify a stable, low-dimensional subspace (the 'load-bearing subspace') that defines the structure. Anomalies are detected when the geometry of the current state deviates significantly from this established structural baseline, signifying structural pressure before observable threshold breaches.
data_sources: The paper uses telemetry data from the Tor anonymity network, specifically focusing on behavioral population data related to network connectivity and topology over time. For financial application, this translates to transactional flow, order book dynamics, or aggregated trading behavior across entities (e.g., high-frequency trading servers, large institutional flows).
alpha_potential: The framework offers significant potential for predicting regime shifts or systemic stress events that precede obvious market crises or volatility spikes. By monitoring the 'load-bearing subspace' of market microstructure or aggregated order flow, a quantitative strategy could detect structural degradation (e.g., hidden liquidity removal, order book instability) before price volatility triggers traditional risk limits. This suggests a leading indicator for short-term, high-risk regime changes, applicable to volatility targeting or dynamic portfolio allocation (barbell strategies).
title_cn: 潜在几何作为结构监测器：特征空间对齐在匿名网络异常检测中的应用
summary_cn: 该研究提出一种利用高维几何变形来监测结构性压力的框架，先于传统阈值警报。其核心思想是通过分析行为群体（如金融交易数据）的稳定结构子空间，提前识别市场结构退化或系统性风险的早期信号。这可用于构建更鲁棒的异常检测系统，识别可能预示市场剧烈波动的“结构压力”，从而调整风险敞口或实施领先的对冲策略。

title: Corrected Integrated Laplace Approximation for Bayesian Inference in Latent Gaussian Models
summary: Latent Gaussian models (LGMs) are a popular class of Bayesian hierarchical models that include Gaussian processes, as well as certain spatial models and mixed-effect models. Efficient Bayesian inference of LGMs often requires marginalizing out the latent variables. For LGMs with a non-Gaussian likelihood, exact marginalization is not possible and a popular approach is to do approximate marginalization with an integrated Laplace approximation (ILA). Using ILA produces an approximate posterior which, in some settings, can differ significantly from the correct posterior, which impacts downstream applications. We propose an importance sampling scheme to correct the error introduced by ILA. By increasing the number of samples in importance sampling, the posterior with ILA converges to the correct posterior. This idea is realized with various techniques, including pseudo-marginalization, quasi-Monte Carlo and randomized quasi-Monte Carlo. We implement our methods in an automatic differentiation framework to support gradient-based algorithms when doing inference on the hyperparameters. For the latter, we specifically consider the use of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo. We demonstrate the benefits of reduced error in various applied models.
core_methodology: The paper proposes an importance sampling scheme to correct approximation errors in Integrated Laplace Approximation (ILA) when performing Bayesian inference for Latent Gaussian Models (LGMs). It leverages techniques like pseudo-marginalization and quasi-Monte Carlo methods, and integrates Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) for hyperparameter optimization within an automatic differentiation framework.
data_sources: The methodology is model-agnostic but is applied to general statistical models, which could include time-series data from financial markets, such as asset returns, volatility measures, or any latent variable structure in financial modeling.
alpha_potential: The primary benefit lies in achieving more accurate posterior inference for complex Bayesian models, specifically LGMs, a class that includes Gaussian Processes. In quantitative finance, accurate Bayesian inference is crucial for robust portfolio optimization, risk modeling (e.g., estimating conditional Value-at-Risk via state-space models), and developing factor models where uncertainty quantification is paramount. Improved accuracy in estimating latent dynamics or model parameters can lead to sharper, more robust trading signals and better downside risk management than standard, less accurate approximations.
title_cn: 用于潜在高斯模型贝叶斯推断的修正积分拉普拉斯近似
summary_cn: 该研究提供了一种修正积分拉普拉斯近似（ILA）中误差的方法，以提高潜在高斯模型（LGMs）的贝叶斯推断精度。这对于金融领域中依赖高斯过程或复杂层次模型的应用至关重要，例如风险管理、投资组合优化和因子模型参数估计。更准确的后验估计能够带来更稳健的风险控制和更可靠的信号生成。

title: Optimized Federated Knowledge Distillation with Distributed Neural Architecture Search
summary: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without centralizing data. However, real-world deployments must simultaneously address statistical heterogeneity across client data (non-IID), system heterogeneity in device capabilities, and communication efficiency. Existing FL approaches mitigate these challenges through improved aggregation, personalization, or knowledge distillation, but they almost universally assume a fixed client architecture, limiting adaptability to heterogeneous data complexity and hardware constraints. This architectural constraint often leads to suboptimal trade-offs between accuracy and efficiency in real-world FL systems. This work introduces FedKDNAS, a distillation-driven FL framework that combines client-side neural architecture selection with distillation of server-coordinated knowledge. Each client autonomously selects a lightweight model under accuracy-resource constraints. It then trains it locally using a hybrid objective combining supervised learning and knowledge distillation and shares only predictions on a public reference set. The server then aggregates and smooths these predictions, optionally combining them with a teacher model, to produce stable distillation targets for the next round. Extensive evaluation on six datasets against six representative FL baselines (FedAvg, Ditto, FedMD, FedDF, FedDistill, Local-KD) demonstrates that FedKDNAS consistently achieves superior Pareto efficiency, improving accuracy by up to 15\% under non-IID conditions, reducing client CPU usage by approximately 28\%, and decreasing communication overhead by up to 44 times while maintaining lightweight logit-based communication.
core_methodology: The paper introduces FedKDNAS, a Federated Learning framework that integrates Neural Architecture Search (NAS) client-side with knowledge distillation from server-coordinated knowledge. Clients autonomously select lightweight models based on resource constraints, train them using a hybrid objective (supervised learning + distillation), and only share predictions on a public reference set. The server aggregates these predictions to form stable distillation targets for the next round. This addresses statistical and system heterogeneity in decentralized ML setups.
data_sources: The methodology is tested on general datasets (e.g., image classification) for FL benchmarks, not explicitly financial data. However, the architecture is designed for situations where diverse datasets (clients) hold proprietary or localized information.
alpha_potential: While the paper itself does not propose a trading strategy, the FedKDNAS framework has significant potential for quantitative finance applications involving decentralized data. For instance, different trading desks, external data vendors, or regional branches might possess localized, non-public market data (e.g., high-frequency order book data, proprietary sentiment feeds). FedKDNAS allows these entities to collaboratively train sophisticated market prediction models without sharing their raw, sensitive data, mitigating privacy concerns while leveraging collective intelligence to potentially improve alpha signal robustness and model generalization across different market regimes or local trading environments.
title_cn: 面向分布式神经架构搜索的优化联邦知识蒸馏
summary_cn: 该方法（FedKDNAS）提出了在去中心化环境中，通过联邦学习结合模型架构搜索和知识蒸馏，训练高性能轻量级模型。这对于需要联合多方私有或本地化金融数据的场景（如不同地区交易团队、异构数据源）具有潜在价值，能有效提升模型准确性、降低计算和通信开销，是构建隐私保护型量化模型的实用框架。

title: Large-Step Training Dynamics of a Two-Factor Linear Transformer Model
summary: Gradient-flow analyses show that simplified linear transformers can learn the in-context linear-regression algorithm, but they do not explain the finite-step behavior of gradient descent at large learning rates. Motivated by empirical work on high-learning-rate transformer instabilities and by the cubic-map phase diagram for quadratic regression, we study an exactly reducible one-prompt linear-transformer training problem. After normalization, the dynamics reduce to a two-factor product map with an effective step-size parameter \(μ\). On the balanced slice, this map recovers the known scalar cubic transition from monotone convergence to catapult convergence, periodic and chaotic bounded nonconvergence, and divergence. We then analyze the full two-dimensional system and show that, for \(0<μ<2\), it has an explicit invariant Chebyshev ellipse separating forward-invariant regions; this ellipse carries off-balanced chaotic dynamics but is transversely repelling, while balanced scalar attractors can be transversely attracting. These results show that large constant learning rates can change the training attractor of the learned transformer rather than merely accelerating convergence: beyond sharp stability thresholds, finite-step training may settle into cycles, bounded chaos, or divergence instead of a single in-context linear-regression solution. We also discuss the consequences for mini-batch gradient descent based training methods.
core_methodology: The paper analyzes the training dynamics of simplified linear transformers using gradient flow analyses, specifically focusing on the effects of large learning rates (represented by an effective step-size parameter μ). It reduces the dynamics to a two-factor product map and explores behaviors like convergence, periodicity, chaos, and divergence based on hyperparameter settings (learning rate/step-size).
data_sources: The research is fundamentally theoretical, analyzing the learning dynamics of the linear transformer model applied to an in-context linear regression task. No specific financial market data is used; the focus is on the stability and convergence properties of the optimization process itself.
alpha_potential: The direct alpha potential is low, as this is a theoretical analysis of optimization stability, not a direct trading signal generator. However, the findings have strong implications for **training robustness** in time-series forecasting models (like Transformers applied to market data). Understanding how large learning rates lead to chaotic dynamics or divergence is crucial for building stable, high-frequency trading/forecasting models where training stability directly impacts predictive accuracy and strategy execution reliability.
title_cn: 二因子线性Transformer模型的大步长训练动力学分析
summary_cn: 该研究深入分析了线性Transformer在采用大步长（高学习率）训练时的优化稳定性。结果表明，过高的学习率可能导致模型训练陷入周期性振荡、有界混沌甚至发散，而非简单的加速收敛。这对将Transformer应用于金融时间序列预测至关重要，因为它揭示了在训练模型时需要避免的超参数阈值，以确保策略预测的稳健性和可靠性。

title: SMoA: Spectrum Modulation Adapter for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
summary: As the number of model parameters increases, parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) has become the go-to choice for tailoring pre-trained large language models. Low-rank Adaptation (LoRA) uses a low-rank update method to simulate full parameter fine-tuning, which is widely used to reduce resource requirements. However, decreasing the rank encounters challenges with limited representational capacity. Theory suggests that LoRA fine-tuning with rank r converges toward the top r singular values of the pre-trained weight matrix. As the rank increases, more principal singular directions are preserved, which generally improves the model's performance. However, a larger rank also introduces more trainable parameters, leading to higher computational cost. To overcome this dilemma, we propose SMoA, a \textbf{S}pectrum \textbf{Mo}dulation \textbf{A}dapter that enlarges the accessible family of spectrum-aware updates under a smaller parameter budget. SMoA partitions the layer into multiple aligned spectral blocks and applies one in-block Hadamard-modulated low-rank branch to each diagonal block, yielding broader coverage of pretrained spectral directions. We provide theoretical analysis and empirical results on multiple tasks. In our experiments, SMoA improves average performance in the current lower-budget setting over LoRA and competitive LoRA-style baselines.
core_methodology: SMoA (Spectrum Modulation Adapter) is a Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) technique designed to improve upon LoRA. It partitions model layers into spectral blocks and applies Hadamard-modulated low-rank updates to each block, aiming to utilize a smaller parameter budget more effectively by capturing broader spectral directions of the pre-trained weights.
data_sources: The paper focuses on general LLM fine-tuning tasks (e.g., classification, generation) and does not specify financial data sources. Application to finance would require financial text data (news, transcripts, reports) or structured numerical data processed by an LLM.
alpha_potential: This method offers efficiency gains in training or updating large models (like LLMs) used for financial tasks such as sentiment analysis, news classification, or generating trade rationale. By fine-tuning these models more efficiently (lower cost, better utilization of limited parameters), quants can rapidly iterate on signals derived from unstructured financial text, potentially leading to faster alpha discovery or more robust NLP models for trading.
title_cn: SMoA：一种用于参数高效微调的频谱调制适配器
summary_cn: SMoA是一种参数高效微调（PEFT）的新方法，旨在克服LoRA在低秩下表示能力受限的问题。它通过频谱分块和哈达玛调制来更有效地利用参数预算。在量化交易中，此技术可用于降低微调大型金融LLM（如处理新闻情感或财报分析）的计算成本，从而加速有效Alpha信号模型的迭代和部署。

title: Beyond Text-to-SQL: An Agentic LLM System for Governed Enterprise Analytics APIs
summary: Enterprise analytics aims to make organizational data accessible for decision-making, yet non-technical users still face barriers when using traditional business intelligence tools or Text-to-SQL systems. While recent Text-to-SQL approaches based on Large Language Models (LLMs) promise natural language access to structured data, they fall short in enterprise settings where analytics pipelines rely on governed APIs rather than raw databases. In practice, these APIs encapsulate complex business logic to ensure consistency, auditability, and security. However, delegating mathematical or aggregation logic to an LLM introduces reliability and compliance risks. To this end, we present Analytic Agent, an LLM-based agentic system that translates natural language intents into secure interactions with enterprise analytics APIs. Evaluated on 90 real enterprise use cases constructed by domain experts, it reliably interprets user goals, validates permissions, executes governed queries, and generates compliant visualizations through multi-step reasoning and policy-aware orchestration.
core_methodology: The core methodology is an agentic LLM system named 'Analytic Agent' designed to translate natural language requests into secure, multi-step interactions with enterprise analytics APIs. It uses policy-aware orchestration and reasoning to validate permissions and execute complex, governed queries, moving beyond simple Text-to-SQL.
data_sources: The system is designed to query structured enterprise analytics data accessible via governed APIs, which encapsulates complex business logic rather than raw databases. This could include validated financial performance metrics, risk exposure data, pre-computed portfolio statistics, or internal compliance logs.
alpha_potential: While the system itself is not an alpha generation strategy, it significantly enhances the efficiency and accessibility of retrieving and analyzing complex, proprietary, or internal financial data locked behind governed APIs. This allows quants and traders to iterate faster on strategy development, backtesting against vetted internal datasets, and gaining rapid insights from complex internal reports without manual intervention or writing extensive data access code. This speed and accessibility act as an operational alpha multiplier.
title_cn: 超越文本到SQL：一个用于受管企业分析API的智能体化LLM系统
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种基于LLM的智能体系统，旨在将自然语言意图安全地转化为对企业分析API（而非原始数据库）的调用。对于量化交易而言，这意味着可以更快速、更合规地访问和分析封装了复杂业务逻辑的内部数据集，加速策略开发和回测，从而提升研究效率和决策速度。

title: Strategy-Induct: Task-Level Strategy Induction for Instruction Generation
summary: Designing effective task-level prompts is crucial for improving the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs). While prior work on instruction induction demonstrates that LLMs can infer better instructions with limited examples, existing approaches often rely on input-output pairs, where obtaining labeled answers can be difficult or costly. To address this limitation, we propose Strategy-Induct, a framework that derives task-level instructions solely from a small set of example questions without requiring labeled answers. Our approach first prompts the model to generate explicit reasoning strategies for each question, forming (strategy, question) pairs. These pairs are then used to induce a task instruction that guides reasoning. Experiments across multiple tasks and model scales demonstrate that Strategy-Induct outperforms state-of-the-art methods in question-only settings. Furthermore, we observe that jointly utilizing LLMs and Large Reasoning Models across task instruction generation and inference may lead to further performance improvements.
core_methodology: Strategy-Induct is a framework for LLM instruction generation that bypasses the need for labeled input-output pairs. It operates by first prompting the LLM to generate explicit reasoning strategies based only on example questions, and then uses these (strategy, question) pairs to induce a final task instruction that guides subsequent inference. This focuses on improving the quality of reasoning derived from context.
data_sources: The methodology is generally applied to textual data (questions and derived strategies) rather than traditional financial market data. In a financial context, this would involve using proprietary market research documents, news articles, analyst reports, or structured financial text to generate analytical instructions for LLMs.
alpha_potential: The direct alpha potential is low as this paper focuses on prompt engineering methodology, not financial signal generation. However, the framework offers significant *indirect* value. By effectively inducing complex reasoning instructions without requiring costly human-labeled financial outcomes (e.g., 'This question implies a long mean-reversion bias in this sector'), Strategy-Induct can significantly improve the accuracy and robustness of LLMs used for tasks like advanced financial document summarization, sentiment extraction from earnings calls, or generating structured trading hypotheses from unstructured data. This leads to better input for quantitative models.
title_cn: Strategy-Induct：面向指令生成的任务级策略归纳
summary_cn: Strategy-Induct 提出了一种新的LLM指令生成框架，仅依赖示例问题（无标签答案）就能推导出有效的任务级指令。该技术可用于提升量化研究中，LLM从非结构化金融文本（如财报、研报）中提取复杂交易逻辑和推理策略的准确性和效率，从而间接增强量化模型的输入质量和决策能力。

title: Markovian Circuit Tracing for Transformer State Dynamic
summary: Many sequence computations are easier to study as movement through internal states than as isolated local circuits. We introduce Markovian Circuit Tracing (MCT), a diagnostic pipeline for testing whether transformer activations contain coarse state-transition structure. The benchmark uses synthetic Hidden Markov Model (HMM) tasks where latent states, transition matrices, Bayesian belief vectors, Bayes-optimal predictions, and forced-state counterfactual targets are known exactly. Across six HMM families and three seeds per family, tiny causal transformers learn near-Bayes next-token predictors, with mean excess loss over Bayes of 0.0138. Residual activations contain partial Bayesian belief information in this controlled synthetic benchmark. State abstractions extracted from these activations recover coarse transition signal, strongest in persistent and lower-state regimes, and weaker in ambiguous-emission and six-state regimes. The clearest result comes from state forcing. Patching a recovered-state centroid reduces KL to the exact HMM counterfactual target from 0.1957 in the unpatched model to 0.0532 on average, beating wrong-state, mean-activation, random-activation, and shuffled-label controls. The contribution is a controlled benchmark and evaluation framework for transformer state-dynamics interpretability, with MCT as a simple reference pipeline
core_methodology: Markovian Circuit Tracing (MCT) is introduced as a diagnostic pipeline to test if transformer activations encode discernible state-transition structures, using synthetic HMM tasks for validation. It focuses on evaluating the interpretability and internal state dynamics of transformers, rather than direct prediction.
data_sources: The paper primarily uses controlled, synthetic Hidden Markov Model (HMM) data for benchmarking the interpretability framework, not financial market data.
alpha_potential: The direct alpha potential is low as the paper focuses on model interpretability within a controlled synthetic environment. However, the methodology provides a strong diagnostic tool for understanding when complex models (like Transformers) successfully learn underlying, structured dynamics. In finance, if a Transformer model trained on market data is shown via MCT to successfully capture latent macro regime transitions or known factor hierarchies, its robustness and interpretability for trading strategy deployment (especially in reinforcement learning or sequence modeling) would be significantly increased. It is a tool for validating 'understanding' in financial models.
title_cn: 基于马尔可夫链路追踪的Transformer状态动力学分析
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种诊断框架MCT，用于测试Transformer内部激活是否编码了潜在的状态转移结构。虽然基于合成数据，但该方法能有效验证Transformer对序列中潜在动态（如宏观市场状态转换）的学习能力。这对于提高金融市场序列预测模型的可解释性和可靠性具有潜在价值，从而增强策略部署的信心。

title: Symmetrization of Loss Functions for Robust Training of Neural Networks in the Presence of Noisy Labels
summary: Labeling a training set is often expensive and susceptible to errors, making the design of robust loss functions for label noise an important problem. The symmetry condition provides theoretical guarantees for robustness to such noise. In this work, we study a symmetrization method arising from the unique decomposition of any multi-class loss function into a symmetric component and a class-insensitive term. In particular, symmetrizing the cross-entropy loss leads to a linear multi-class extension of the unhinged loss. Unlike in the binary case, the multi-class version must have specific coefficients in order to satisfy the symmetry condition. Under suitable assumptions, we show that this multi-class unhinged loss is the unique convex multi-class symmetric loss. We also show that it has a fundamental local role: the linear approximation of any symmetric loss around score vectors with equal components is equivalent to the multi-class unhinged loss. We then introduce SGCE and alpha-MAE, two loss functions that interpolate between the multi-class unhinged loss and the Mean Absolute Error while allowing control of the beta-smoothness of the loss. Experiments on standard noisy-label benchmarks show competitive performance compared with existing robust loss functions.
core_methodology: The core methodology introduces 'symmetrization' as a technique to make loss functions robust to noisy labels based on theoretical symmetry conditions. Specifically, it derives a unique convex multi-class symmetric loss, equivalent to a multi-class unhinged loss, and proposes new losses (SGCE, alpha-MAE) interpolating between this new loss and MAE.
data_sources: The paper uses standard benchmark datasets for classification tasks (e.g., CIFAR, Fashion-MNIST) to test label noise robustness. In a trading context, this methodology would be applied to labeled data sets, such as datasets where event labels (e.g., market up/down, volatility regimes) are derived or annotated, which are inherently noisy due to market complexity.
alpha_potential: The direct application is improving the robustness of supervised machine learning models used in trading (e.g., classification of future price movements, regime detection) when the training data labels are imperfect or noisy. If a trading model is trained on noisy labels (e.g., based on imperfect indicators or back-tested historical outcomes), losses derived from this research (like the multi-class unhinged loss or SGCE) could significantly enhance model stability and generalization performance compared to standard cross-entropy, leading to more reliable trading signals.
title_cn: 含噪标签下神经网络鲁棒训练的损失函数对称化
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种基于损失函数对称性的方法，用于提高神经网络在处理含噪声标签数据时的鲁棒性。对于训练数据标签存在误差的金融时间序列预测任务（如价格方向分类或市场状态识别），采用论文提出的对称化损失函数（如多类别Un-hinged Loss的推广），可有效减轻标签噪声影响，从而提升模型预测的稳定性和可靠性，间接增强量化策略的有效性。

title: FedCoE: Bridging Generalization and Personalization via Federated Coordinated Dual-level MoEs
summary: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for privacy-preserving distributed learning. However, existing FL methods face a fundamental challenge. Traditional averaging-based approaches suffer from parameter divergence under non-IID conditions, while personalized FL methods overfit to local data and fail to generalize to new clients (cold-start problem). Mixture-of-Experts naturally addresses this by routing heterogeneous data to specialized experts rather than forcing uniform aggregation. In this paper, we propose FedCoE, a Federated Coordinated dual-level mixture-of-Experts framework that effectively balances global generalization with local personalization. FedCoE maintains multiple independent global expert models on the server and employs a shared gating network to dynamically model client-expert correlations during aggregation, effectively mitigating expert drift and gating inconsistency. To address the cold-start challenge, we introduce an adaptive mechanism that enables new clients to immediately leverage the global expert pool without extensive local training. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedCoE achieves 78.00% global accuracy and 89.32% personalized accuracy on average, outperforming the baseline by 8.82% and 29.19%, respectively. In cold-start scenarios, FedCoE delivers 77.27% accuracy without any local fine-tuning, outperforming baselines by over 12.54%.
core_methodology: Federated Coordinated Dual-level Mixture-of-Experts (FedCoE) framework for balancing global generalization and local personalization in distributed learning environments.
data_sources: Distributed client data (general machine learning datasets implied, not specific financial data)
alpha_potential: The paper focuses on privacy-preserving distributed learning and model generalization across heterogeneous clients, which is a general ML engineering improvement rather than a direct alpha generation technique for trading.

title: A Unified Framework for Uncertainty-Aware Explainable Artificial Intelligence: A Case Study in Power Quality Disturbance Classification
summary: Post-hoc explainable AI (XAI) methods typically produce deterministic attribution maps, whereas Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) induce a distribution over explanations. Capturing the variability of this distribution is important for uncertainty-aware decision-making. This paper formalises the \emph{explanation distribution} as the push-forward measure of the BNN posterior through any Lipschitz-continuous attribution operator. It further proposes the uncertainty-aware relevance attribution operator (UA-RAO), a general family of operators that summarises the explanation distribution using the mean, variance, coefficient of variation, quantiles, and set-theoretic aggregation measures. Theoretical support is provided through Monte Carlo accessibility and Wasserstein approximation bounds. The framework is evaluated on a 15-class power quality disturbance (PQD) classification benchmark, comparing three BNN approximations paired with three attribution operators using relevance mass accuracy and intersection-over-union as localisation metrics. Results show that deep ensembles with the mean UA-RAO improve localisation over the deterministic baseline, while other UA-RAO summaries reveal uncertainty patterns absent from point-estimate attributions. Qualitative results on measured signals further suggest that these patterns generalise beyond the synthetic training distribution. The framework is domain-agnostic and can be applied to any BNN paired with a Lipschitz-continuous attribution operator.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a Unified Framework (UA-RAO) to quantify the uncertainty surrounding Explainable AI (XAI) attributions by modeling the 'explanation distribution' derived from Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs). It uses measures like variance and quantiles to summarize this uncertainty.
data_sources: The framework is tested on a Power Quality Disturbance (PQD) classification benchmark. The methodology is domain-agnostic and designed for general BNNs and attribution operators.
alpha_potential: The direct application to financial trading is low as the case study is in power engineering. However, the core technique—quantifying and utilizing the *uncertainty* inherent in model explanations (XAI attribution maps)—is highly relevant for high-stakes financial applications where model robustness and explainability are critical (e.g., regulatory reporting, risk management, or model debugging). This helps assess *how much to trust* an explanation, which can be mapped to trading confidence.

title: Concentration of General Stochastic Approximation Under Heavy-Tailed Markovian Noise
summary: We establish maximal concentration bounds for the iterates generated by stochastic approximation algorithms with general step sizes, where the noise has a finite-state Markovian component plus a Martingale-difference component. When the Martingale-difference noise is bounded, we show that the tail of the error can be sub-Gaussian, sub-Weibull, or something lighter than any Pareto but heavier than any Weibull, depending on the step size sequence and on whether the random operator is almost surely contractive, almost surely non-expansive, or expansive with positive probability. Our analysis relies on a novel Lyapunov function involving the moment-generating function of the solution to a Poisson equation, together with an auxiliary projected algorithm. We complement the upper bounds with worst-case examples showing that qualitatively sharper bounds are impossible. We further study the case of unbounded Martingale-difference noise when the average operator is contractive, and the step sizes are of order $1/k$. In this setting, we show that if the random operator is almost surely non-expansive, then the error tail is at most three times heavier than the noise tail, whereas if the random operator is expansive with positive probability, then the error may have substantially heavier tails. These results are obtained through a novel black-box truncation argument that reduces the unbounded-noise setting to the bounded-noise case.
core_methodology: The paper analyzes the convergence properties and concentration bounds for iterates in general Stochastic Approximation (SA) algorithms, particularly focusing on scenarios where the noise involves both Markovian components and Martingale-difference noise, potentially unbounded.
data_sources: The analysis is theoretical, focusing on the properties of general stochastic processes and algorithms, not specific financial market data.
alpha_potential: While stochastic approximation is fundamental to many iterative optimization methods used in Reinforcement Learning (RL) and adaptive signal processing in finance, this paper provides foundational theoretical convergence results rather than a direct trading strategy. It could inform the robustness of adaptive trading systems or parameter estimation in complex models, but the direct alpha generation is far removed.

title: A Sharper Picture of Generalization in Transformers
summary: We study transformers' generalization behavior on boolean domains from the perspective of the Fourier Spectra of their target functions. In contrast to prior work (Edelman et al., 2022; Trauger and Tewari, 2024), which derived generalization bounds from Rademacher complexity, we investigate the feasibility of obtaining generalization bounds via PAC-Bayes theory. We show that sparse spectra concentrated on low-degree components enable low-sharpness constructions with good generalization properties. Our idea is to show the existence of flat minima implementing any boolean function of sparsity no greater than the context length, and then apply a PAC-Bayes bound to an idealized low-sharpness learner, resulting in a non-vacuous generalization bound. We evaluate predictions empirically and conduct a mechanistic interpretability study to support the realism of our theoretical construction in real transformers.
core_methodology: Theoretical study of Transformer generalization bounds using Fourier Spectra analysis and PAC-Bayes theory, focusing on the relationship between output function sparsity and generalization sharpness.
data_sources: Boolean domains for theoretical analysis; empirical evaluation uses real Transformer predictions, likely on benchmark tasks, not direct financial data.
alpha_potential: The insights primarily concern the theoretical generalization capabilities of Transformers. While understanding generalization is crucial for deploying complex ML models in finance (e.g., ensuring robustness), this paper does not propose a trading strategy or address financial data specifics.

title: Winfree Oscillatory Neural Network
summary: Oscillations and synchronization are widely believed to play a fundamental role in representation and computation. However, existing machine learning approaches based on synchronization dynamics have largely been confined to specialized settings such as object discovery, with limited evidence of scalability to standard vision benchmarks or logic reasoning tasks. We propose the Winfree Oscillatory Neural Network (WONN), a dynamical neural architecture based on generalized Winfree dynamics. WONN evolves representations on the torus $(S^1)^d$ through structured oscillatory interactions, combining phase-based inductive biases with flexible and hierarchical interaction mechanisms instantiated as either fixed trigonometric mappings or learnable neural networks. We evaluate WONN on image recognition and complex reasoning tasks, including CIFAR, ImageNet, Maze-hard, and Sudoku. Across these domains, WONN achieves competitive or superior performance with strong parameter efficiency. In particular, WONN is, to our knowledge, the first synchronization-based oscillatory architecture to scale competitively to ImageNet-1K. Furthermore, on Maze-hard, WONN achieves 80.1% accuracy using only 1% of the parameters of prior state-of-the-art models. These results suggest that structured oscillatory dynamics provide a scalable and parameter-efficient alternative to conventional neural architectures.
core_methodology: The paper introduces the Winfree Oscillatory Neural Network (WONN), a dynamical neural architecture based on generalized Winfree dynamics that evolves representations using structured oscillatory interactions on the torus $(S^1)^d$.
data_sources: Standard computer vision benchmarks (CIFAR, ImageNet) and logical reasoning tasks (Maze-hard, Sudoku).
alpha_potential: The methodology focuses on novel neural network architectures optimized for efficiency and achieving strong performance on vision/logic tasks. While the superior parameter efficiency and novel dynamics could lead to advantages in developing resource-constrained or time-series specialized models for finance, the direct application is not immediately obvious without adaptation to sequential/non-stationary financial data, limiting immediate practical value.

title: Task-Routed Mixture-of-Experts with Cognitive Appraisal for Implicit Sentiment Analysis
summary: Implicit sentiment analysis is challenging because sentiment toward an aspect is often inferred from events rather than expressed through explicit opinion words. Existing models typically learn from the final polarity label, which provides limited guidance for reasoning about sentiment from the context. Motivated by cognitive appraisal theory, we propose an appraisal-aware multi-task learning (MTL) framework for implicit sentiment analysis that provides polarity prediction with two complementary auxiliary tasks: implicit sentiment detection and cognitive rationale generation. However, training several objectives with different targets and sharing a single backbone across tasks in MTL limits flexibility and can lead to task interference. To reduce interference among these related but distinct objectives, we adopt task-level mixture-of-experts models in which all tasks share a common set of experts, and task identity controls the sparse combination of these experts. Our method builds on an encoder-decoder architecture and replaces a subset of encoder and decoder blocks with these sparse mixtures. We use a task-conditioned router to select sparse expert mixtures for each task, and a task-separated routing objective to encourage different tasks to learn distinct expert-selection patterns. Experimental results show that our model outperforms recently proposed approaches, with strong gains on the implicit sentiment subset. Our code is available at https://github.com/yaping166/TRMoE-ISA.
core_methodology: The core methodology involves a Task-Routed Mixture-of-Experts (TRMoE) framework combined with Cognitive Appraisal Theory for implicit sentiment analysis. It uses a multi-task learning (MTL) approach with auxiliary tasks (implicit sentiment detection and cognitive rationale generation) to enhance the main sentiment prediction task, using sparse expert routing to minimize task interference.
data_sources: Textual data, likely social media or news articles, focusing on unstructured text for implicit sentiment detection.
alpha_potential: The model significantly improves the accuracy of implicit sentiment analysis, which is crucial for processing unstructured text data (like news, reports, or social media) in finance. While the paper focuses on general NLP tasks, the improved ability to detect nuanced, inferred sentiment could be directly applied to news-based alpha strategies (e.g., trading based on latent market sentiment extracted from news narratives) where explicit sentiment signals are insufficient.

title: Beyond Numerical Features: CNN-Driven Algorithm Selection via Contour Plots for Continuous Black-Box Optimization
summary: The present paper introduces a new representation-driven approach to per-instance algorithm selection, applied to black-box optimization, for automatically choosing the most promising solver from a fixed portfolio. Prior work in continuous optimization largely relies on numerical descriptors, including Exploratory Landscape Analysis features and learned embeddings such as Deep-ELA. This work studies a complementary representation: contour-map visualizations of probed landscapes. A CNN regressor takes multiple instance-specific contour views (stacked or encoded per view and aggregated) and predicts per-solver performance, enabling selection by the predicted best value. On the standard BBOB 2009 single-objective protocol, the resulting selectors significantly outperform the single best solver (SBS) and are competitive with feature-based baselines. A subsequent bi-objective evaluation under the DeepELA setting further indicates that the same image-based principle can be competitive when using windowed contour views. Overall, the results suggest that simple vision models can exploit spatial structure in probed landscapes for algorithm selection without handcrafted ELA features.
core_methodology: Using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) regressor to predict the best-performing algorithm solver for a given black-box optimization problem, based on visual representations (contour plots) of the probed landscape rather than traditional numerical features.
